terms.d: An ordered array of numbers representing a point, direction or magnitude in a vector space.
A rectangular two-dimensional array of numbers encoding a linear map between vector spaces.
A multidimensional array generalising scalars, vectors and matrices to any number of indices.
A set of vectors closed under addition and scalar multiplication over a field.
A linearly independent set of vectors whose span is the entire vector space.
Property of a vector set in which no member is a linear combination of the others.
The number of linearly independent columns of a matrix, equal to its independent rows.
The set of all vectors that a matrix maps to the zero vector.
The span of a matrix's columns; every vector reachable as a matrix-vector product.
Sum of element-wise products of two equal-length vectors, producing a scalar.
Product of a column vector with a row vector, producing a rank-one matrix.
Element-wise multiplication of two arrays of identical shape.
Block product forming a large matrix from all pairwise entry products of two matrices.
Notation specifying tensor products and contractions by labelling and repeating axis indices.
The sum of the diagonal entries of a square matrix, equal to the eigenvalue sum.
Scalar giving the signed volume scaling factor of the linear map a square matrix defines.
The matrix that composes with a given square matrix to yield the identity.
Generalised inverse defined for any matrix, giving minimum-norm least-squares solutions.
Real square matrix whose transpose equals its inverse, preserving lengths and angles.
Symmetric matrix whose quadratic form is non-negative for every vector.
Scalar factor by which a linear map stretches its associated eigenvector.
Nonzero vector whose direction is unchanged when a given linear map is applied.
Non-negative scalar giving the stretch factor along a principal axis of a linear map.
Matrix of all pairwise inner products between a collection of vectors.
Fitting criterion that minimises the sum of squared residuals between model and data.
Space spanned by repeated matrix applications to a vector, underlying iterative linear solvers.
Iterative solver for symmetric positive-definite linear systems using mutually conjugate search directions.
Factorisation of a diagonalisable matrix into eigenvectors, a diagonal eigenvalue matrix, and the eigenvector inverse.
Result guaranteeing every real symmetric matrix has an orthonormal eigenbasis with real eigenvalues.
Factorisation of any matrix into two orthogonal matrices and a diagonal matrix of singular values.
SVD retaining only the largest singular values, yielding the optimal fixed-rank approximation.
Approximate SVD using random projections to sketch a matrix's dominant subspace cheaply.
Result proving truncated SVD gives the best low-rank approximation in Frobenius and spectral norms.
Factorisation of a square matrix into lower and upper triangular factors, usually with row permutation.
Factorisation of a matrix into an orthonormal matrix and an upper triangular matrix.
Factorisation of a symmetric positive-definite matrix into a triangular factor times its transpose.
Factorisation of a square matrix into a unitary matrix and an upper triangular matrix.
Factorisation of a matrix into an orthogonal factor and a positive semi-definite factor.
Low-rank factorisation built from actual selected columns and rows of the original matrix.
Low-rank factorisation expressing all columns of a matrix through a chosen subset of them.
Factorisation of a non-negative matrix into two non-negative low-rank factors.
Orthogonal transformation projecting data onto successive directions of maximal variance.
Expression of a tensor as a sum of rank-one outer products.
Factorisation of a tensor into a small core tensor multiplied by a factor matrix per mode.
Representation of a high-order tensor as a chain of low-order core tensors.
Approximation of a large curvature matrix as a Kronecker product of two smaller matrices.
Function assigning non-negative length to vectors, satisfying homogeneity, triangle inequality and positive definiteness.
Family of norms given by the p-th root of summed absolute values raised to p.
Sum of the absolute values of a vector's components.
Square root of the sum of squared components; ordinary Euclidean length.
The largest absolute value among a vector's components.
Count of nonzero entries in a vector; not a true norm.
Square root of the sum of all squared entries of a matrix.
Largest singular value of a matrix; its maximum stretching factor on unit vectors.
Sum of a matrix's singular values, used as a convex surrogate for rank.
Distance function satisfying non-negativity, symmetry, identity of indiscernibles and the triangle inequality.
Distance family parameterised by an order p, generalising Manhattan and Euclidean distance.
Distance scaled by the inverse covariance matrix, accounting for correlation between dimensions.
Inner product of two vectors divided by the product of their L2 norms.
Number of positions at which two equal-length sequences differ.
Ratio of intersection size to union size between two sets.
Phenomenon where data becomes sparse and pairwise distances concentrate as dimensionality grows.
Instantaneous rate of change of a function with respect to its input.
Derivative of a multivariate function with respect to one variable, holding others fixed.
Vector of all first partial derivatives, pointing in the direction of steepest increase.
Rate of change of a function along a specified direction vector.
Matrix of all first-order partial derivatives of a vector-valued function.
Matrix of all second-order partial derivatives of a scalar function.
Rule for differentiating composed functions by multiplying the derivatives of their stages.
Local polynomial approximation of a function built from its derivatives at a point.
Property bounding how fast a function can change between any two input points.
Property that a function's gradient is Lipschitz continuous, placing a bound on curvature.
Point at which the gradient of a function equals zero.
Stationary point that is a minimum in some directions and a maximum in others.
Result giving derivatives of variables defined implicitly by a system of equations.
Conventions and identities for differentiating scalar, vector and matrix functions of matrix arguments.
Rule relating probability densities under an invertible transformation via the Jacobian determinant.
Computing exact derivatives by applying the chain rule to a program's elementary operations.
Automatic differentiation propagating derivative information alongside values from inputs towards outputs.
Automatic differentiation propagating derivatives backwards from outputs, efficient for scalar objectives with many inputs.
Reverse-mode automatic differentiation applied to compute neural network loss gradients.
Numbers carrying a nilpotent infinitesimal component, used to implement forward-mode differentiation.
Forward-mode operation applying a Jacobian to a tangent vector without materialising it.
Reverse-mode operation applying a transposed Jacobian to a cotangent vector without materialising it.
Product of a Hessian with a vector computed without forming the full Hessian.
Directed acyclic graph of elementary operations recording a computation so derivatives can be propagated.
Memory-saving strategy that discards intermediate activations and recomputes them during the backward pass.
Numerical derivative estimate formed from function evaluations at nearby input points.
Verification of analytic gradients by comparison against finite-difference estimates.
Gradient surrogate that passes gradients unchanged through a non-differentiable operation.
Technique computing gradients through differential equation solutions by integrating an adjoint system backwards.
Measurable function assigning numerical values to outcomes of a random experiment.
Function giving the probability that a discrete random variable takes each specific value.
Function whose integral over a region gives the probability a continuous variable falls there.
Function giving the probability that a random variable is at most a given value.
Inverse of the cumulative distribution function, mapping probabilities to values.
Distribution describing the simultaneous behaviour of two or more random variables.
Distribution of a subset of variables obtained by summing or integrating out the rest.
Probability of an event given that another event is known to have occurred.
Identity expressing a posterior probability in terms of likelihood, prior and evidence.
Property where the joint distribution of variables factorises into the product of marginals.
Property where two variables are independent once a third variable is known.
Probability-weighted average value of a random variable.
Expected squared deviation of a random variable from its mean.
Expected product of two variables' deviations from their means, measuring joint variability.
Expectation of a power of a random variable, characterising distribution shape.
Identity stating the expectation of a conditional expectation equals the unconditional expectation.
Result that sample averages converge to the population mean as sample size grows.
Result that sums of many independent variables approach a normal distribution.
Stochastic process whose next state depends only on the current state.
Distribution over states left unchanged by a Markov chain's transition operator.
Bound limiting the probability that a random quantity deviates far from its expectation.
Result relating the expectation of a convex function to the function of the expectation.
Collection of random variables indexed by time or another ordering parameter.
Stochastic process where every finite collection of values has a multivariate normal distribution.
Unobserved random variable inferred from observed data within a probabilistic model.
Distribution over a single binary outcome with a fixed success probability.
Distribution of the number of successes in a fixed number of independent Bernoulli trials.
Distribution over a single draw from a finite set of mutually exclusive outcomes.
Distribution of category counts across a fixed number of independent categorical draws.
Distribution of counts of independent events occurring at a constant average rate.
Distribution of the number of trials until the first success in repeated Bernoulli trials.
Distribution of trials needed to reach a fixed number of successes; models overdispersed counts.
Distribution assigning equal probability density or mass across a bounded range.
Symmetric bell-shaped continuous distribution parameterised by mean and variance.
Vector-valued Gaussian distribution parameterised by a mean vector and covariance matrix.
Distribution of a variable whose logarithm is normally distributed.
Continuous distribution of waiting times between events in a Poisson process.
Continuous positive distribution with shape and rate parameters, generalising the exponential.
Continuous distribution on the unit interval, commonly used for probabilities.
Distribution over probability simplices, the multivariate generalisation of the beta distribution.
Distribution of the sum of squared independent standard normal variables.
Heavy-tailed distribution arising when estimating a normal mean with unknown variance.
Distribution of a ratio of two scaled chi-squared variables, used in variance comparisons.
Heavy-tailed symmetric distribution with undefined mean and variance.
Symmetric distribution with exponential tails, peaked at its location parameter.
Extreme-value distribution of the maximum of many independent samples.
Power-law distribution with heavy tails, describing scale-free magnitudes.
Class of distributions whose density factorises into natural parameters and sufficient statistics.
Distribution formed as a weighted combination of several component distributions.
Sum of observed values divided by the number of observations.
Middle value of an ordered dataset, splitting it into equal halves.
Most frequently occurring value in a dataset or the density peak of a distribution.
Value below which a specified proportion of a distribution or dataset falls.
Difference between the seventy-fifth and twenty-fifth percentiles of a dataset.
Square root of the variance, expressing spread in the units of the data.
Division by n minus one when estimating variance, removing downward bias.
Standardised third moment measuring asymmetry of a distribution.
Standardised fourth moment measuring tail weight and peakedness of a distribution.
Value expressed as the number of standard deviations from the mean.
Robust dispersion measure given by the median of absolute deviations from the median.
Normalised covariance measuring the strength of a linear relationship between two variables.
Correlation computed on ranks, measuring monotonic association between variables.
Non-parametric estimate of a density formed by summing smoothing kernels at data points.
Rule computing an estimate of a population parameter from sample data.
Difference between an estimator's expected value and the true parameter value.
Property that an estimator converges in probability to the true parameter as samples grow.
Statistic carrying all sample information about a parameter.
Expected curvature of the log-likelihood, quantifying how much data informs a parameter.
Lower bound on the variance of any unbiased estimator, given by inverse Fisher information.
Probability of observed data viewed as a function of model parameters.
Parameter estimation by maximising the likelihood of the observed data.
Parameter estimation by maximising the posterior density, combining likelihood with a prior.
Parameter estimation by equating sample moments to theoretical moments.
Interval estimate whose construction covers the true parameter at a specified long-run rate.
Standard deviation of an estimator's sampling distribution.
Resampling procedure estimating an estimator's distribution by sampling the data with replacement.
Resampling procedure estimating bias and variance by systematically leaving out one observation.
Split of expected prediction error into squared bias, variance and irreducible noise.
Default claim of no effect or no difference that a test attempts to reject.
Claim accepted when evidence is sufficient to reject the null hypothesis.
Quantity computed from data whose distribution under the null hypothesis is known.
Probability of observing data at least as extreme as observed, assuming the null hypothesis.
Pre-specified threshold controlling the tolerated probability of a false rejection.
Rejecting a null hypothesis that is actually true; a false positive.
Failing to reject a null hypothesis that is actually false; a false negative.
Probability that a test correctly rejects a false null hypothesis.
Standardised magnitude of a difference or association, independent of sample size.
Test comparing means using a t-distributed statistic under normality assumptions.
Test comparing means across multiple groups by partitioning total variance.
Test of independence or goodness of fit for categorical count data.
Non-parametric test comparing distributions of two independent samples using ranks.
Non-parametric test comparing paired observations using signed ranks of differences.
Non-parametric test comparing empirical distribution functions via their maximum discrepancy.
Test comparing nested models through the ratio of their maximised likelihoods.
Test building a null distribution by randomly reshuffling labels among observations.
Inflation of false positives that arises when many hypotheses are tested together.
Probability of making at least one false rejection across a family of tests.
Expected proportion of false rejections among all rejected hypotheses.
Multiple-testing adjustment dividing the significance threshold by the number of tests.
Step-up procedure ranking p-values to control the false discovery rate.
Inference remaining statistically valid under continuous monitoring and optional stopping.
Non-negative evidence measure with expectation at most one under the null, supporting anytime-valid testing.
Distribution-free framework producing prediction sets with guaranteed marginal coverage.
Probability distribution encoding beliefs about parameters before observing data.
Updated distribution over parameters after conditioning on observed data.
Probability of observed data with parameters integrated out under the prior.
Prior whose family is preserved in the posterior for a given likelihood.

Model where parameters themselves have priors governed by higher-level hyperparameters.

Ratio of marginal likelihoods used to compare two competing models.
Distribution of new observations obtained by averaging the likelihood over the posterior.
Interval containing a specified posterior probability mass for a parameter.
Approximating a posterior by optimising over a tractable family of distributions.

Set containing the entire line segment between any two of its points.
Function whose graph lies below any chord joining two points on it.

Minimisation of objectives with multiple local minima and no global optimality guarantee.
Optimisation of a linear objective subject to linear equality and inequality constraints.
Optimisation of a quadratic objective subject to linear constraints.
Convex optimisation over matrices constrained to be positive semi-definite.

Difference between the optimal primal and dual objective values.

Geometry of an objective function over parameter space, including minima, saddles and flat regions.

Scalar controlling the size of each parameter update step.

Rescaling or truncating gradients exceeding a threshold to bound update magnitude.
Transforming an optimisation problem's geometry to reduce its effective condition number.
Optimisation seeking parameters whose neighbourhood has uniformly low loss.
Averaging iterates across training steps to reduce variance in the final parameters.
Stochastic methods using control variates on past gradients to lower estimator variance.
Optimisation using only function evaluations, estimating descent directions without gradients.
Derivative-free optimisation perturbing parameters randomly and reweighting by observed fitness.
Global optimisation of expensive black-box functions using a surrogate model and acquisition function.
Equality or inequality condition restricting which parameter values are admissible.
Set of all parameter values satisfying every constraint of an optimisation problem.
Gradient descent followed by projection of each iterate back onto the feasible set.
Converting constraints into objective terms that grow with the degree of violation.

Mapping real-valued tensors onto integer grids using scale and zero-point parameters.

Loss of a value because its magnitude exceeds or falls below the representable range.
Severe relative error arising when subtracting two nearly equal approximate numbers.
Factor by which a problem amplifies input perturbations into output error.
Property of an algorithm whose computed result is close to the exact result for nearby input.
Assessing an algorithm by the size of input perturbation for which its output is exact.
Summation algorithm tracking a running correction term to reduce accumulated rounding error.
Recursive divide-and-conquer summation reducing error growth compared with sequential accumulation.
Subtracting the maximum before exponentiating to compute log-sum-exp without overflow.
Training with low-precision compute while retaining higher-precision copies for sensitive accumulations.
Multiplying the loss before backpropagation so small gradients remain representable in low precision.
Higher-precision parameter copies updated by the optimiser alongside low-precision compute copies.
Property that summation order changes results, causing non-determinism in parallel reductions.
Estimating quantities by averaging over randomly generated samples.

Deterministic algorithm producing number sequences with statistical properties resembling randomness.

Drawing from a proposal distribution and accepting samples with probability proportional to a density ratio.

Partitioning the domain into strata and sampling within each to reduce estimator variance.
Integration using deterministic low-discrepancy sequences instead of independent random samples.

Design ensuring each input dimension is stratified evenly across its range.

uncertain: Whether Muon, SOAP and Shampoo have moved from research use into default production LLM training optimisers by 2026, or whether AdamW remains the standard; I did not verify adoption, only that all are actively studied.

Whether the MXFP4 (32-value blocks, power-of-two scale) and NVFP4 (16-value blocks, E4M3 scale) specifications hold beyond the Blackwell hardware generation; I list the generic 'Microscaling (MX) formats' term rather than asserting vendor-specific block sizes as stable.
HiFloat8 (HiF8) appeared in search results as an 8-bit format with tapered mantissa, but I could not confirm it is a standardised or widely implemented format, so it is excluded.
Whether 'always-valid inference' or 'anytime-valid inference' is the settled canonical name for the e-value/sequential-testing family; both are in current use.
Whether 'e-process' should be listed as a separate term from 'e-value'; the distinction is real in the literature but I could not confirm it is standard curriculum vocabulary.

Optional copy-and-patch just-in-time compiler that translates hot interpreter traces into machine code at runtime.

uncertain: Current maintenance status of Vaex — it is a real out-of-core Python dataframe library, but I could not verify whether it is still actively developed in 2026, so I left it out of the term list.
Petastorm (Parquet-to-tensor dataset library) — appears to be archived/unmaintained, but I could not confirm its status, so it is excluded.
Apache Flume — I could not confirm whether it has formally moved to the Apache Attic, only that Kafka Connect and modern ingestion tools have displaced it. Excluded rather than annotated incorrectly.
The pandas/dataframe interchange protocol (__dataframe__) — I could not verify whether it is now formally deprecated in favour of the Arrow PyCapsule interface, so it is excluded.
Kafka diskless topics (KIP-1150) — I found no confirmation that this has shipped in a stable Kafka release, so it is excluded.
Exact GA status of Kafka share groups (queues, KIP-932): reported as early access in 4.0, preview in 4.1, with production-ready targeted for 4.2. I have included the term but not its release status.
Prefect's announced acquisition of Dagster Labs was reported as not yet closed, with both products continuing independently. I therefore added no deprecation note to either Prefect or Dagster.
Astral's 'ty' type checker and the 'nab' Python locking project are referenced in 2026 sources but appear pre-1.0; I excluded both rather than assert stable tooling.
Whether pip-tools should now carry a superseded note — it is still published, but uv's pip compile/sync is the recommended path for new projects. I excluded the term rather than annotate ambiguously.

uncertain: DAMA-DMBOK 3.0 is described in 2026 vendor sources as in active development; I could not verify a published release date from DAMA International itself.
DuckLake's current version and production readiness: sources report v0.3 as of late 2025 with ecosystem support largely limited to DuckDB and MotherDuck; I did not verify a 2026 version number.
Whether the Data Contract Specification (datacontract.com) and ODCS have formally converged; ODCS was at v3.1.0 under Bitol at the time of checking, but I could not confirm the very latest version.
The Singer tap/target specification's current maintenance status; I omitted it rather than assert it is active or dormant.
Datafold's current commercial status could not be verified, so it is not listed as a tool.
re_data (open-source dbt data reliability package) appears low-activity; I could not confirm whether it is maintained in 2026.
Apache Atlas is still an Apache project; my note that it is 'largely superseded' reflects analyst commentary about non-Hadoop stacks, not an official deprecation.
Hive Metastore and Apache Hive are not formally deprecated; the notes reflect their legacy status in new lakehouse deployments rather than an end-of-life announcement.

Exact scope of Iceberg v3 adoption per engine varies; some v3 features (deletion vectors, row lineage, variant) reached general availability on different platforms at different dates during 2025-2026.
Whether Apache Gravitino and Lakekeeper have reached Apache top-level or 1.0 stability respectively was not verified; Apache Polaris graduation to top-level was confirmed for early 2026.

terms.d: Learning a mapping from inputs to known target labels using a dataset of labelled training pairs.

Paradigm that stores training data and defers computation until prediction time.

Model with a fixed number of parameters independent of training set size.

Model that estimates the conditional distribution of the target given the features.
Model that estimates the joint distribution of features and target, allowing sampling of data.

Supervised task assigning each instance to exactly one of three or more classes.

Agreement between two raters or label sets corrected for agreement expected by chance.
Chance-corrected inter-rater agreement statistic for more than two raters.
General reliability coefficient for rater agreement across arbitrary measurement scales and missing data.
Sensitivity plus specificity minus one, summarising a single operating point.
Negative average log probability the model assigns to the true class.
Plot of true positive rate against false positive rate across all decision thresholds.
Probability that a randomly chosen positive is scored above a randomly chosen negative.

Rescaled discrimination measure equal to twice AUC minus one.
Maximum separation between cumulative score distributions of positives and negatives.

Evaluation plotting net benefit of a model against threshold probability.
Precision measured at the threshold that achieves a required recall level.
Property whereby predicted probabilities match observed empirical event frequencies.
Plot of observed event frequency against predicted probability, grouped into bins.
Weighted average absolute gap between confidence and accuracy across probability bins.
Largest absolute confidence-accuracy gap across probability bins.
Calibration error computed over equal-count rather than equal-width probability bins.

Calibration mapping each score bin to its empirical positive rate.
Concentration of predictive distributions, independent of whether those predictions are calibrated.
Splitting a proper score into calibration, resolution and intrinsic uncertainty components.

Allowing a model to abstain when its confidence falls below a threshold.
Plot of error rate against the fraction of inputs a selective predictor answers.

Average absolute difference between predicted and actual numeric values.
Average absolute error expressed as a percentage of the actual value.
Percentage error variant dividing by the mean of actual and predicted magnitudes.
Total absolute error divided by total actual volume across all observations.
Mean absolute error scaled by that of a naive seasonal forecast.

Proportion of target variance explained by the model relative to the mean.

Average of the reciprocal rank of the first relevant result per query.
Mean across queries of average precision over the ranked result list.
Sum of graded relevance discounted logarithmically by result position.
DCG divided by the DCG of the ideal ranking for that query.
