modules.module: Deep learning fundamentals, training and systems

terms.d: Basic unit computing a weighted sum of inputs plus a bias, then applying a nonlinear activation.
Feedforward network of stacked fully connected layers separated by nonlinear activation functions.
Group of units applying one parameterised transformation to an input tensor inside a network.
Learnable scalar scaling an input connection, adjusted during training to reduce the loss.
Learnable additive offset applied to a unit's weighted sum before its activation function.
Linear output of a unit before the activation function is applied to it.
Layer in which every output unit connects to every input unit through a learnable weight matrix.
Layer applying learnable filters that slide across the input, sharing weights across spatial positions.
Layer carrying a hidden state across sequence positions and reusing the same weights each step.
Recurrent cell using input, forget and output gates plus a cell state to retain long-range information.
Recurrent cell with update and reset gates, simpler than LSTM and using fewer parameters.
Identity shortcut adding a block's input to its output so gradients flow through deep stacks.
Unnormalised real-valued network outputs passed to softmax or sigmoid to obtain probabilities.
Directed graph of tensor operations recording how outputs depend on inputs and parameters.
Result that sufficiently wide one-hidden-layer networks approximate any continuous function on a compact domain.
Sharing a single parameter matrix between two layers, typically input embedding and output projection.
Assumptions embedded in an architecture that make some hypotheses easier to learn than others.
Elementwise nonlinearity applied to a layer's pre-activations, giving the network non-linear expressive power.
Activation squashing any real input into the open interval between zero and one.
Zero-centred sigmoidal activation mapping real inputs into the interval between minus one and one.
Piecewise-linear approximation of the sigmoid, cheaper to evaluate on constrained hardware.
Activation returning the input when positive and zero otherwise.
ReLU variant with a small fixed positive slope for negative inputs instead of zero.
Leaky ReLU whose negative-region slope is a learned parameter rather than a fixed constant.
Leaky ReLU whose negative slope is sampled randomly during training and fixed at inference.
ReLU clipped at an upper bound of six, keeping activations in a fixed low-precision-friendly range.
Activation squaring the ReLU output, producing sparser and sharper responses in feedforward blocks.
Activation that is linear for positive inputs and a saturating exponential for negative inputs.
Scaled ELU variant whose fixed constants drive activations toward zero mean and unit variance.
ELU reparameterisation that remains continuously differentiable at the origin for all slope settings.
Activation weighting an input by the standard normal cumulative distribution evaluated at that input.
Activation multiplying the input by its own sigmoid, giving a smooth non-monotonic curve.
Piecewise-linear approximation of SiLU using a hard sigmoid, designed for mobile inference.
Smooth self-gated activation multiplying the input by the tanh of its softplus.
Smooth everywhere-positive approximation of ReLU given by the logarithm of one plus the exponential.
Sigmoidal activation dividing the input by one plus its absolute value, saturating polynomially.
Activation returning the maximum over several parallel linear projections of the same input.
Periodic activation adding a squared sine term to the identity, aiding extrapolation of periodic signals.
Trainable piecewise activation obtained by integrating learned affine transformations applied to the ELU function.
Layer multiplying one linear projection elementwise by a sigmoid-gated second projection of the same input.
Gated linear unit variant whose gating branch uses GELU instead of the sigmoid.
Gated linear unit variant whose gating branch uses SiLU, standard in modern transformer feedforward blocks.
Gated linear unit variant whose gating branch uses ReLU.
Gated linear unit with no nonlinearity on the gate, multiplying two linear projections directly.
Function turning a logit vector into a probability distribution via normalised exponentials.
Numerically stable logarithm of softmax, used directly with negative log-likelihood objectives.
Softmax alternative projecting logits onto the probability simplex, allowing exactly zero probabilities.
Parameterised family interpolating between softmax and sparsemax, controlling output sparsity by an exponent.
Continuous relaxation of categorical sampling permitting gradients to flow through discrete choices.
Choice of starting parameter values, controlling signal and gradient scale at the first training steps.
Counts of incoming and outgoing connections of a unit, used to set initialisation variance.
Initialisation principle setting weight variance inversely to layer width to preserve signal magnitude.
Variance scaling using the average of fan-in and fan-out, suited to symmetric saturating activations.
Variance scaling by fan-in with a factor of two, matched to rectifier activations.
Variance scaling by fan-in alone, the basis for self-normalising SELU networks.
Initialising weight matrices as orthogonal matrices to preserve gradient norms through depth.
Gaussian initialisation with samples beyond a cutoff resampled, avoiding extreme starting weights.
Data-dependent scheme rescaling orthogonally initialised layers so each layer's output has unit variance.
Depth-aware rescaling of residual branches that enables stable deep training without normalisation layers.
Initialising a learnable scalar gate on each residual branch to zero, starting the network as identity.
Per-channel learnable scaling initialised near zero on residual branch outputs, stabilising very deep transformers.
Dividing residual branch outputs by a function of depth so accumulated variance stays bounded.
Width-dependent scaling of initialisation, learning rates and multipliers keeping feature updates stable as width grows.
Practice of tuning hyperparameters on a small model and transferring them to a wider one under muP.
Layer rescaling and recentring activations using computed statistics to stabilise optimisation.
Normalising each feature using mean and variance computed across the current mini-batch, then applying learned affine parameters.
Proposed phenomenon where a layer's input distribution changes as preceding layers update during training.
Moving averages of batch mean and variance accumulated during training and used at inference.
Batch normalisation computing statistics across all data-parallel devices rather than per-device batches.
Computing batch statistics over fixed-size virtual sub-batches independent of the actual batch size.
Normalising each sample across its feature dimension, independent of batch size or composition.
Layer normalisation variant rescaling by root mean square only, omitting mean subtraction and the bias.
Normalising each sample and each channel separately across spatial dimensions.
Normalising within fixed groups of channels per sample, independent of batch size.
Reparameterising each weight vector into a learned direction and an independently learned magnitude.
Dividing a weight matrix by its largest singular value to bound the layer's Lipschitz constant.
Normalising each activation by the summed squares of neighbouring channel activations.
terms.n: Superseded by batch and layer normalisation; effectively unused in modern architectures.

terms.d: Residual block placing the normalisation layer before the sublayer, leaving the skip path unnormalised.
Residual block placing the normalisation layer after adding the sublayer output to the skip path.
terms.n: Largely superseded by pre-norm for deep transformers, which trains stably without careful warmup.

terms.d: Applying normalisation both before and after a residual sublayer to bound its output magnitude.
Post-norm scheme scaling the residual path by a depth-dependent constant, enabling very deep transformers.
Normalising an activation vector to a single learned global scale rather than per-feature parameters.
Normalising query and key vectors before attention scoring to prevent attention logits from growing unbounded.
Normalisation replacement applying a scaled tanh with learned parameters instead of computing activation statistics.
Instance normalisation whose affine scale and shift are predicted from a conditioning signal.
Preprocessing that rescales input features to zero mean and unit variance before the first layer.
Scalar function measuring disagreement between predictions and targets, minimised during training.
Training principle of minimising average loss over the observed training sample.
Regression loss averaging squared differences between predictions and targets.
Regression loss averaging absolute differences between predictions and targets, less sensitive to outliers.
Regression loss that is quadratic near zero error and linear beyond a threshold.
Asymmetric regression loss whose minimiser is a specified conditional quantile of the target.
Classification loss equal to the negative log probability the model assigns to the true class.
Cross-entropy specialised to two-class or independent multi-label targets with sigmoid outputs.
Loss equal to the negative log probability a model assigns to observed data.
Cross-entropy reweighted to down-weight easy examples, addressing severe class imbalance.
Margin-based classification loss penalising predictions that fall inside a fixed decision margin.
Loss measuring the information lost when one probability distribution approximates another.
Objective based on optimal transport distance between distributions, used in generative adversarial training.
Objective pulling paired representations together and pushing unpaired representations apart in embedding space.
Objective enforcing that an anchor is closer to a positive than to a negative by a margin.
Contrastive objective classifying the true positive against sampled negatives using a temperature-scaled similarity softmax.
Classification loss adding an angular margin between feature and class-weight directions on a hypersphere.
Sequence loss summing over all alignments between an unsegmented input and a shorter target sequence.
Segmentation loss derived from the Dice overlap coefficient between predicted and true masks.
Segmentation or detection loss derived from the overlap ratio between predicted and true regions.
Objective comparing deep features of generated and target images rather than raw pixel values.
Variational objective bounding log marginal likelihood by a reconstruction term minus a divergence term.
Auxiliary penalty on the softmax log-partition function that keeps output logits from drifting large.
Penalty encouraging mixture-of-experts routers to distribute tokens evenly across experts.
Loss scaling each class's contribution inversely to its frequency to counter imbalance.
Algorithm computing loss gradients for all parameters by applying the chain rule backward through the graph.
Calculus rule expressing the derivative of composed functions as a product of local derivatives.
Vector of partial derivatives of a scalar objective with respect to all parameters.
Matrix of first partial derivatives of a vector-valued function with respect to its vector input.
Matrix of second partial derivatives of a scalar objective, describing local curvature.
Technique computing exact derivatives of programs by composing derivatives of their elementary operations.
AD mode propagating derivatives from outputs backward, efficient when outputs are few and inputs many.
AD mode propagating derivatives from inputs forward, efficient when inputs are few and outputs many.
Primitive of reverse-mode AD multiplying a cotangent row vector by a function's Jacobian.
Primitive of forward-mode AD multiplying a function's Jacobian by a tangent direction vector.
Curvature probe computing the Hessian times a vector without materialising the full Hessian matrix.
Ordered record of executed operations and intermediates that reverse-mode AD replays backward.
Execution model building the differentiation graph dynamically as the program runs.
Verification comparing analytic gradients against finite-difference estimates to detect implementation errors.
Trick passing gradients unchanged through a non-differentiable operation during the backward pass.
Operation blocking gradient flow through a tensor while leaving its forward value unchanged.
Applying backpropagation to a recurrent network unrolled across all sequence timesteps.
Backpropagation through time limited to a fixed window of recent timesteps to bound cost.
Algorithm mapping gradients and internal state to parameter updates that reduce the loss.
Iterative method stepping parameters in the direction opposite the loss gradient.
Gradient descent using gradients estimated from randomly sampled mini-batches rather than the full dataset.
Accumulating an exponentially decayed running average of gradients to damp oscillation and accelerate descent.
Momentum variant evaluating the gradient at the anticipated look-ahead position.
Adaptive method dividing each step by the square root of accumulated squared gradients.
AdaGrad variant using a decaying window of squared gradients and updates, removing the global learning rate.
Adaptive method dividing steps by the root of an exponentially decayed average of squared gradients.
Optimiser combining exponential moving averages of gradients and squared gradients with bias correction.
Adam with weight decay applied directly to parameters rather than folded into the gradient.
Adam incorporating Nesterov-style look-ahead in its first-moment term.
Adam variant using a non-decreasing maximum of second-moment estimates to restore convergence guarantees.
Adam variant rectifying the adaptive term's variance early in training, reducing the need for warmup.
Adam variant replacing the second-moment norm with an infinity norm over past gradients.
Memory-efficient adaptive optimiser factorising second-moment statistics into row and column vectors.
Layer-wise adaptive rate scaling setting per-layer step sizes from weight-to-gradient norm ratios.
Layer-wise trust-ratio scaling applied on top of Adam, enabling very large batch training.
Optimiser producing sign-based updates from an interpolated momentum, storing only one state tensor per parameter.
Optimiser updating parameters using only the elementwise sign of the gradient.
Second-order optimiser using a clipped, intermittently estimated diagonal Hessian as a preconditioner.
Optimiser orthogonalising momentum-based updates for hidden weight matrices before applying them.
Iterative matrix procedure approximating the orthogonal polar factor without computing a singular value decomposition.
Structure-aware preconditioner maintaining separate matrix statistics for each dimension of a weight tensor.
Implementation sharding Shampoo's preconditioner computation and state across data-parallel ranks.
Optimiser running Adam inside Shampoo's eigenbasis, improving stability and reducing preconditioner update frequency.
Approximation of the Fisher information matrix as a Kronecker product, giving tractable natural-gradient steps.
Method preconditioning gradients by the inverse Fisher information, making steps invariant to parameterisation.
Quasi-Newton method approximating inverse curvature from a limited history of gradient and parameter differences.
Transforming the gradient by a matrix that rescales directions to improve the effective conditioning.
Optimiser storing moment states in eight-bit quantised form to cut optimiser memory.
Optimiser using iterate averaging and interpolation so no explicit learning-rate decay schedule is required.
Wrapper periodically interpolating slow weights toward fast weights produced by an inner optimiser.
Averaging parameters sampled along the training trajectory to find flatter, better-generalising solutions.
Maintaining a decayed running average of parameters, used for evaluation instead of raw weights.
Objective minimising loss in a neighbourhood of the parameters, biasing training toward flat minima.
Scalar controlling how far parameters move along the update direction at each step.
Rule varying the learning rate over training steps according to a predetermined shape.
Opening phase raising the learning rate from near zero to its peak over a fixed step count.
Schedule multiplying the learning rate by a constant factor at fixed step milestones.
Schedule multiplying the learning rate by a fixed factor at every step.
Schedule scaling the learning rate by the reciprocal square root of the step count.
Schedule decaying the learning rate along a half cosine curve to a small final value.
Cyclic schedule repeatedly resetting the learning rate to a high value and annealing it again.
Three-phase schedule holding a constant peak learning rate between a warmup and a final decay.
Final decay segment of a schedule during which most of the loss improvement is realised.
Schedule raising the learning rate to a peak and then annealing far below the starting value.
Schedule oscillating the learning rate between fixed lower and upper bounds throughout training.
Assigning progressively smaller learning rates to layers closer to the input during fine-tuning.
Heuristic scaling the learning rate proportionally with the global batch size.
Pathology where gradients shrink toward zero through depth, stalling learning in early layers.
Pathology where gradient magnitudes grow without bound through depth, producing destructive parameter updates.
Rescaling or truncating gradients that exceed a threshold before the optimiser applies them.
Clipping with a threshold derived from parameter or gradient-history statistics rather than a fixed constant.
Adaptive clipping method detecting gradient-norm anomalies by z-score against a running distribution.
Failure mode where a rectifier unit outputs zero for all inputs and stops receiving gradient.
Abrupt large increase in training loss that can precede divergence during large-model pretraining.
Training failure in which the loss grows without recovering, often ending in numerical overflow.
Degeneracy where representations across tokens or depth converge toward a low-dimensional subspace.
Instability where attention distributions become near one-hot, causing sharp gradients and training breakdown.
Bounding logits through a scaled tanh so they cannot grow into numerically unstable ranges.
Stationary point that is a minimum along some directions and a maximum along others.
Distinction between low-curvature and high-curvature solutions, often linked to differing generalisation behaviour.
Regime where curvature rises until it sits at the largest value the learning rate tolerates.
Statistic estimating the batch size beyond which gradient estimates stop becoming meaningfully less noisy.
Delayed generalisation where validation performance jumps long after training accuracy has saturated.
Phenomenon where test error falls, rises near the interpolation threshold, then falls again with more capacity.
Any technique constraining a model or its training to reduce overfitting and improve generalisation.
Penalty proportional to the sum of absolute parameter values, driving some weights exactly to zero.
Penalty proportional to the sum of squared parameter values, shrinking all weights toward zero.
Multiplicative shrinkage of parameters applied at each update step.
Applying weight decay directly to parameters rather than through the adaptive gradient preconditioner.
Randomly zeroing a fraction of units during training so the network cannot rely on any single one.
Dropout implementation rescaling surviving activations during training so inference needs no adjustment.
Regulariser randomly zeroing individual weights rather than whole unit activations.
Randomly skipping entire residual branches during training, leaving the identity path intact.
Dropout applied to attention probability weights before they multiply the value vectors.
Halting training once validation performance stops improving for a set number of evaluations.
Expanding training data by applying label-preserving transformations to existing examples.
Augmentation training on convex combinations of two inputs and their correspondingly mixed labels.
Augmentation pasting a patch from one image into another and mixing labels by patch area.
Augmentation masking out a contiguous random region of the input during training.
Replacing hard one-hot targets with slightly softened distributions to reduce overconfidence.
Projecting each weight vector back inside a fixed norm ball after every update.
Keeping dropout active at inference and averaging samples to obtain predictive uncertainty estimates.
Condition where a model fits training data closely but performs poorly on unseen data.
Condition where a model is too constrained to capture structure present in the training data.
Difference between a model's performance on training data and on held-out data.
One complete pass of the training procedure over the entire training dataset.
Subset of training examples whose gradients are averaged into a single parameter update.
Number of examples whose gradients contribute to one parameter update.
Sub-division of a batch processed in one forward and backward pass before accumulation.
Total examples contributing to one update across all devices and accumulation steps combined.
One iteration comprising forward pass, backward pass and a single optimiser parameter update.
Summing gradients over several micro-batches before updating, simulating a larger batch within fixed memory.
Component that batches, shuffles and prefetches training examples, feeding the accelerator without stalls.
Partitioning data into sets used respectively for fitting, model selection and final unbiased evaluation.
Saved snapshot of parameters, optimiser state and step count allowing training to resume.
Fixing random sources and kernel selection so a training run reproduces bitwise identical results.
Concatenating short sequences into full-length training samples to avoid wasting compute on padding.
Empirical power-law relation predicting loss from model size, dataset size and training compute.
Allocating a fixed compute budget between parameters and tokens to minimise final loss.
Systematic search over hyperparameter configurations to identify the best-performing training setup.
Sequence training that feeds ground-truth previous tokens rather than the model's own predictions.
Reusing representations learned on one task or dataset to improve learning on another.
Initial large-scale training phase producing general-purpose representations before any task-specific adaptation.
Continuing training of a pre-trained model on task-specific data to adapt its parameters.
Adaptation strategy holding pre-trained feature-extractor weights fixed while training only new output layers.
Fine-tuning schedule progressively unfreezing layers from the output end toward the input.
Evaluating frozen representations by fitting only a linear classifier on top of them.
Extending pre-training of an existing checkpoint on new domain or language data.
Adjusting a model so it performs well on a target distribution differing from its training distribution.
Training one model jointly on several tasks with shared parameters and combined objectives.
Ordering training examples from easier to harder rather than presenting them uniformly at random.
Curriculum whose difficulty ordering is derived from the model's own current loss on each example.
Specified proportions in which distinct data sources are sampled during a training run.
Late-training phase upweighting high-quality data while the learning rate decays.
Loss of previously acquired capabilities when a model is trained further on new data.
Continual-learning penalty anchoring parameters important to earlier tasks, weighted by Fisher information.
Training a smaller student model to reproduce the outputs or internal signals of a larger teacher.
Larger or better-performing model whose behaviour supplies training signal to a student.
Smaller model trained to match a teacher's behaviour under a distillation objective.
Full teacher probability distributions used as training targets instead of hard one-hot labels.
Scaling factor applied to logits that controls how smooth the teacher's soft targets become.
Distillation matching only the teacher's final output logits or probabilities.
Distillation matching intermediate hidden representations between teacher and student layers.
Distillation matching relationships among examples or layers rather than individual activation values.
Distillation where teacher and student share the same architecture, often the model's own earlier checkpoint.
Distillation in which teacher and student are trained simultaneously rather than from a frozen teacher.
Distillation training the student on teacher-generated output sequences rather than per-token distributions.
Distillation scoring the student's own sampled outputs with the teacher, avoiding train-inference mismatch.
Distillation using synthesised or teacher-inverted inputs when the original training data is unavailable.
Compressing a dataset into a small synthetic set on which training approximates full-data results.
Removing parameters, channels or layers from a trained network to reduce size and computation.
Zeroing individual weights anywhere in a tensor, producing irregular sparsity patterns.
Removing whole architectural units such as channels, heads or layers, shrinking dense tensor shapes.
Pattern requiring exactly N nonzeros in every group of M consecutive weights.
Semi-structured pattern keeping two nonzeros per four consecutive weights, accelerated by sparse tensor cores.
Removing the weights with smallest absolute value as a saliency proxy.
Pruning by how weights move away from zero during fine-tuning rather than by final magnitude.
Pruning criterion using inverse-Hessian information to remove weights and compensate remaining ones.
One-shot layer-wise pruning method solving a local reconstruction problem with approximate second-order information.
One-shot pruning scoring weights by magnitude times input activation norm, requiring no weight updates.
Structured removal of entire convolutional filters or feature channels from a layer.
Structured removal of individual attention heads found to contribute little to model output.
Removing whole transformer blocks or layers to shorten the network.
Alternating pruning and retraining over several rounds to reach high sparsity with less accuracy loss.
Conjecture that dense networks contain sparse subnetworks trainable in isolation to comparable accuracy.
Resetting surviving weights to an early-training value before retraining a pruned subnetwork.
Accelerator unit that skips zero operands in N:M sparse matrix multiplications for extra throughput.
Training at fixed sparsity while periodically dropping and regrowing connections during the run.
Replacing a weight matrix with the product of two thinner matrices to cut parameters and compute.
Compression pipeline structurally pruning a model then recovering accuracy through distillation from the original.
Bit width and encoding used to represent tensor values, trading accuracy against speed and memory.
Single-precision floating point with eight exponent and twenty-three mantissa bits.
Tensor-core format with FP32 exponent range and reduced mantissa, accumulating results in FP32.
Half-precision floating point with five exponent bits, offering high mantissa precision but narrow dynamic range.
Sixteen-bit format keeping FP32's eight exponent bits and truncating the mantissa, so loss scaling is unnecessary.
Eight-bit floating point used for matrix multiplication inputs with higher-precision accumulation.
FP8 encoding with four exponent and three mantissa bits, favouring precision over range.
FP8 encoding with five exponent and two mantissa bits, favouring dynamic range over precision.
Four-bit floating point with two exponent and one mantissa bit, always paired with block scaling.
Open specification pairing narrow element types with a shared scale factor per fixed-size block.
Microscaling FP8 recipe sharing one power-of-two scale across each block of thirty-two elements.
Microscaling FP4 format with thirty-two-element blocks sharing a power-of-two exponent scale.
NVIDIA FP4 format with sixteen-element blocks and an FP8 scale factor, giving finer granularity than MXFP4.
Eight-bit signed integer representation used for quantised weights and activations.
Running most operations in a narrow format while keeping selected computations and master state wider.
Framework feature automatically choosing per-operation precision and inserting the required casts.
Multiplying the loss before backward so small gradients survive representation in a narrow float format.
Higher-precision copy of parameters updated by the optimiser and cast down for each forward pass.
Rounding probabilistically in proportion to distance, so repeated low-precision updates remain unbiased.
Training with simulated quantisation in the forward pass so weights adapt to low-precision deployment.
Assigning a shared scale factor to a small contiguous group of tensor elements.
FP8 recipe deriving the current scale factor from a history of past tensor amax values.
NVIDIA library implementing FP8 and FP4 transformer layers with automatic scaling management.
Splitting a training workload across multiple accelerators or hosts that coordinate through collective communication.
Replicating the model across devices, giving each a different data shard and averaging their gradients.
Data-parallel implementation replicating full parameters per rank and all-reducing gradients during the backward pass.
Splitting individual weight matrices across devices so each computes a slice of one layer.
Assigning consecutive groups of layers to different devices that process micro-batches in sequence.
Idle accelerator time at pipeline fill and drain when no micro-batch is available to process.
Pipeline schedule alternating one forward and one backward micro-batch to bound activation memory.
Assigning each device several non-contiguous layer chunks to shrink the pipeline bubble.
Schedule splitting backward into input and weight gradient stages to fill pipeline idle slots.
Distributing mixture-of-experts feedforward experts across devices and routing tokens to them.
Sharding activations of non-tensor-parallel operations along the sequence dimension to cut activation memory.
Partitioning the sequence across devices for attention itself, enabling contexts exceeding one device's memory.
Context-parallel attention passing key and value blocks around a device ring while overlapping computation.
Combining data, tensor and pipeline parallelism simultaneously across a multi-dimensional device grid.
Family of stages partitioning optimiser states, gradients and parameters across data-parallel ranks to remove replication.
ZeRO level sharding parameters themselves, gathering each layer's weights only while it is in use.
Extension moving optimiser state and its update step to host CPU memory.
PyTorch strategy sharding parameters, gradients and optimiser state, gathering weights per unit on demand.
Per-parameter-sharded rewrite of FSDP built on DTensor, composing cleanly with tensor parallelism.
Sharding parameters within device groups while replicating and all-reducing across groups.
Discarding intermediate activations in the forward pass and recomputing them during backward to save memory.
Recomputing only cheap operations while keeping expensive intermediates stored, tuning the memory-compute trade-off.
Moving activations to host memory between forward and backward, streaming them back when needed.
Splitting optimiser moment tensors across ranks so no device holds the full state.
Collective combining values from all ranks and delivering the identical result to every rank.
Bandwidth-optimal all-reduce implemented as a reduce-scatter followed by an all-gather around a device ring.
Collective in which every rank receives the concatenation of all ranks' contributed shards.
Collective reducing values across ranks and giving each rank one distinct slice of the result.
Collective where each rank sends a distinct block to every other rank, used for expert routing.
Grouping gradient tensors into fixed-size buffers so communication starts before the backward pass finishes.
Issuing collectives asynchronously so network transfers proceed while the accelerator continues computing.
Reducing gradient communication volume through quantisation, sparsification or low-rank approximation.
Slow rank that delays a synchronous collective and stalls the entire training step.
Running a job that continues correctly as workers join or leave the cluster.
Logical multi-dimensional arrangement of devices onto which parallelism strategies are mapped.
PyTorch distributed tensor abstraction carrying explicit sharding and replication placements over a device mesh.
Training library providing ZeRO sharding, offloading, pipeline parallelism and memory-efficient optimisers.
NVIDIA library of composable tensor, pipeline, sequence and expert parallel transformer building blocks.
PyTorch-native reference codebase demonstrating composable multi-dimensional parallelism for large model pretraining.
NVIDIA library implementing topology-aware collective communication primitives for multi-GPU and multi-node jobs.
Ring-all-reduce distributed training framework layered over multiple deep learning frameworks.
terms.n: In maintenance mode; new work generally uses native FSDP, DeepSpeed or Megatron-Core instead.

terms.d: Method letting workers take several independent steps before averaging parameters, reducing communication frequency.
Low-communication distributed training using infrequent outer optimiser steps over locally trained replicas.
Specialised processor built for the dense linear algebra that dominates neural network workloads.
Accelerator unit executing small matrix multiply-accumulate operations at reduced precision.
GPU compute cluster containing cores, registers, shared memory and schedulers that executes thread blocks.
Group of GPU threads scheduled and executed together in lockstep.
Small fast on-chip memory explicitly managed by kernels to stage reused tiles.
Stacked off-chip DRAM providing an accelerator's main high-throughput working memory.
Rate at which data moves between an accelerator's compute units and its main memory.
Structural limit where memory bandwidth, not arithmetic throughput, bounds achievable performance.
High-bandwidth point-to-point interconnect linking accelerators within a node or scale-up domain.
Low-latency high-throughput network fabric commonly used for inter-node accelerator communication.
Memory holding intermediate forward-pass tensors retained for use in the backward pass.
Single accelerator program launched over many threads to perform one tensor operation.
Combining several operations into one kernel so intermediates stay on chip instead of returning to memory.
Mechanism capturing a sequence of kernel launches and replaying it to remove per-launch CPU overhead.
Ratio of active warps to the maximum a multiprocessor supports, limited by register and memory use.
Partitioning a computation into blocks sized to fit fast memory, maximising data reuse.
Python-embedded language for writing tiled GPU kernels without direct low-level programming.
PyTorch compiler tracing models into graphs and generating fused kernels ahead of execution.
Compiler that fuses and optimises tensor graphs into hardware-specific executables.
Rate of training work completed per unit time, measured in tokens, samples or steps per second.
Single floating-point operation, the unit in which model compute cost is counted.
Ratio of useful model FLOPs achieved to the accelerator's theoretical peak, excluding recomputation.
Ratio of all executed FLOPs, including recomputation, to theoretical peak throughput.
Performance model bounding a kernel by memory bandwidth or peak compute depending on its arithmetic intensity.
Ratio of arithmetic operations performed to bytes moved between compute units and memory.
Regime where a kernel's runtime is limited by arithmetic throughput rather than data movement.
Regime where a kernel's runtime is limited by memory bandwidth rather than arithmetic throughput.
Wall-clock duration of one complete training iteration, the primary throughput measurement.
Fraction of elapsed cluster time spent on useful training progress rather than failures, restarts or stalls.
Time-ordered profiler record of kernels, collectives and host activity used to locate stalls.
NVIDIA system-wide profiler visualising kernel, memory and communication activity over time.
Built-in PyTorch tool recording operator timings, memory use and exportable execution traces.

uncertain: Derf, described in one late-2025 source as a Dynamic Tanh successor using a scaled error function: could not verify the name, paper or any adoption, so excluded.
Whether Horovod is formally archived or only in maintenance under LF AI as of 2026 — the note says maintenance mode, but the precise governance status is unverified.
PSGD / Kron preconditioned-gradient optimisers: the research line is real, but I could not confirm the canonical 2026 naming or adoption level, so they were excluded from the optimiser family.
HBM4 shipping status in production training accelerators during 2026 — I listed only the generic HBM term rather than a specific generation.

Exact deprecation timeline for FSDP1 versus FSDP2: sources say FSDP2 is the PyTorch 2.6+ default with FSDP1 kept for compatibility and receiving no new features, but no formal removal date was confirmed, so no deprecation note was attached.
'5D parallelism' appears informally in some 2026 writing; I could not confirm it as a canonical term and used '3D parallelism' plus the individual axes instead.
Whether 'sandwich normalisation' or 'peri-layer normalisation' is now the preferred canonical name for pre-and-post residual normalisation.
AdaGC (adaptive per-tensor gradient clipping) is real and published, but I could not verify production adoption, so only the generic 'adaptive gradient clipping' entry and ZClip were included.

terms.d: Feedforward network of stacked fully connected layers separated by nonlinear activations.
Layer in which every output unit is a learned weighted sum of all input units.
Network whose connections form a directed acyclic graph, passing activations forward without recurrence.
Trainable lookup table mapping discrete tokens or categories to dense continuous vectors.
Layer multiplying one linear projection elementwise by a gated nonlinear transform of a second projection.
Gated linear unit using a Swish-activated gate, the standard feedforward block in modern transformers.
Gated linear unit variant whose gating branch uses the GELU activation.
Narrow intermediate layer forcing information through a reduced-dimension representation.
Vision architecture alternating token-mixing and channel-mixing MLPs over image patches, using neither convolution nor attention.
Attention-free block combining channel MLPs with a spatial gating unit that mixes across tokens.
Network placing learnable univariate spline functions on edges instead of fixed activations on nodes.
Network that generates the weights of a second target network from a conditioning input.
Permutation-invariant architecture encoding each set element independently then aggregating with a symmetric pooling function.
Two-branch architecture with tied weights that compares inputs through distances between their embeddings.
Layer standardising activations using mini-batch statistics, then rescaling with learned affine parameters.
Layer standardising activations across the feature dimension of each individual example.
Normalisation dividing activations by their root-mean-square without mean subtraction, with a learned scale.
Normalisation computing statistics over groups of channels, independent of batch size.
Residual block ordering that normalises inputs before each sublayer, stabilising deep transformer training.
Normalising query and key vectors before attention to bound logit magnitude and prevent training divergence.
Conditioning mechanism predicting normalisation scale and shift from an external signal such as diffusion timestep.
Network built from layers that apply learned filters slid across spatially or temporally structured input.
Layer computing cross-correlations between an input tensor and a bank of learned local filters.
Small learned weight tensor convolved across the input to produce one output channel.
Step size by which a convolution or pooling window advances, controlling output spatial resolution.
Convolution with gaps between kernel taps, enlarging receptive field without extra parameters or downsampling.
Learned upsampling layer that maps each input element to a spatially larger output patch.
Factorisation of convolution into a per-channel spatial filter followed by a pointwise channel mixer.
Convolution with unit spatial extent that mixes and reprojects channels at each position.
Convolution splitting input channels into groups filtered independently, reducing parameters and computation.
Convolution whose sampling positions are shifted by learned per-location offsets.
Convolution masked so each output depends only on current and earlier positions.
Block expanding channels, applying depthwise convolution, then projecting back, with a residual across the narrow ends.
Module recalibrating channels by pooling global context and predicting per-channel multiplicative gates.
Module applying sequential channel and spatial attention gates to a convolutional feature map.
Multi-branch block concatenating outputs of parallel convolutions at several kernel sizes plus pooling.
Property whereby shifting the input shifts the feature map correspondingly, arising from weight-shared convolution.
Reuse of the same parameters at many input positions or timesteps within a layer.
Layer aggregating each local neighbourhood into a single value, reducing spatial resolution.
Pooling that outputs the largest activation within each window.
Pooling that outputs the mean activation within each window.
Pooling that collapses each entire feature map to its mean, producing one value per channel.
Module pooling features at multiple grid resolutions and concatenating them into a fixed-length vector.
Operation extracting fixed-size features from an arbitrary region proposal using bilinear interpolation.
Upsampling that rearranges channel values into a higher-resolution spatial grid.
Region of the input that can influence one unit's activation in a given layer.
Subregion of the theoretical receptive field that actually carries significant gradient influence, typically Gaussian-shaped.
Architecture fusing multi-resolution backbone features top-down to produce a scale-aware feature hierarchy.
Early convolutional network for digit recognition alternating convolution, subsampling and fully connected layers.
Deep convolutional network that won ImageNet 2012 using ReLU activations, dropout and GPU training.
Deep convolutional network built uniformly from stacked 3x3 convolutions and max pooling.
Convolutional network stacking inception modules with dimensionality-reducing 1x1 convolutions and auxiliary classifiers.
Convolutional network replacing inception modules entirely with depthwise separable convolutions.
Convolutional network stacking residual blocks with identity shortcuts, enabling very deep trainable models.
ResNet variant whose blocks aggregate many parallel grouped-convolution branches of identical topology.
Convolutional network where each layer receives the concatenated outputs of all preceding layers in its block.
Efficient convolutional family for mobile inference built on depthwise separable and inverted residual blocks.
Efficient convolutional network using grouped pointwise convolutions with channel shuffling for cross-group information flow.
Convolutional family scaling depth, width and input resolution jointly by a single compound coefficient.
Convolutional family whose layer widths and depths follow quantised linear rules found by design-space search.
Convolutional network modernised with transformer-inspired choices: large depthwise kernels, LayerNorm, inverted bottlenecks, GELU.
Encoder-decoder convolutional network with skip connections linking matching-resolution contracting and expanding paths.
Network with no dense layers, producing dense spatial predictions at pixel resolution.
Segmentation architecture using atrous spatial pyramid pooling to capture multi-scale context at fixed resolution.
Single-stage object detector predicting boxes and classes directly on a dense grid in one pass.
Two-stage detector extending region-proposal detection with a parallel per-region segmentation-mask branch.
Autoregressive audio network stacking dilated causal convolutions with gated activations and residual connections.
Sequence architecture of dilated causal convolutions with residual blocks, used instead of recurrence.
Architecture consuming raw point clouds via shared per-point MLPs and a symmetric max-pooling aggregation.
Network with cyclic connections that carries a hidden state across sequence positions.
Simple recurrent network feeding the previous hidden layer back as additional input at each step.
Recurrent cell with an additive memory cell and multiplicative gates that mitigates vanishing gradients.
LSTM's additive memory channel that carries information across timesteps with minimal transformation.
LSTM gate deciding what fraction of the previous cell state is retained.
LSTM gate controlling how much of the candidate update is written into the cell state.
LSTM gate controlling how much of the cell state is exposed as the hidden state.
Recurrent cell with update and reset gates and no separate memory cell.
Architecture running separate forward and backward recurrences and combining both hidden states per position.
Reservoir-computing model with a fixed random recurrent layer where only the readout is trained.
Sequence model interleaving parallel convolutions with a minimal elementwise recurrent pooling step.
Recurrent cell whose gate computations drop hidden-state dependence, allowing highly parallel training.
Modernised LSTM family adding exponential gating and matrix memory, with sLSTM and mLSTM blocks.
xLSTM block replacing scalar memory with a parallelisable matrix memory updated by outer products.
Architecture pairing a controller network with an external memory matrix accessed by differentiable read and write heads.
Memory-augmented network extending the Neural Turing machine with dynamic memory allocation and temporal link tracking.
Sequence model whose output distribution is attention over input positions rather than a fixed vocabulary.
Two-part design where an encoder compresses the input and a decoder generates the output conditioned on it.
Encoder-decoder framework mapping a variable-length input sequence to a variable-length output sequence.
Attention scoring queries and keys with a small feedforward network before softmax normalisation.
Attention scoring queries and keys by dot product, optionally with a learned bilinear matrix.
Attention that selects discrete positions stochastically rather than forming a weighted average.
Attention where queries, keys and values all derive from the same sequence.
Attention where queries come from one sequence and keys and values from another.
The three learned projections of a token that determine attention scoring and the retrieved content.
Attention computing softmax over query-key dot products divided by the square root of head dimension.
One independent attention computation over a low-dimensional projected subspace of the representation.
Attention running several heads in parallel and concatenating their outputs through a learned projection.
Attention mask preventing each position from attending to later positions, enforcing autoregressive factorisation.
Architecture built entirely from stacked self-attention and feedforward sublayers with residual connections and normalisation.
Repeating unit containing an attention sublayer and a feedforward sublayer, each wrapped in residual normalisation.
Two-layer MLP applied independently and identically to every token representation in a transformer block.
Transformer using bidirectional attention over the whole input to produce contextual representations.
Transformer using causal attention to model sequences autoregressively from left to right.
Transformer pairing a bidirectional encoder with a causal decoder that cross-attends to encoder outputs.
Stored key and value tensors from previous positions, reused so autoregressive decoding avoids recomputation.
Initial tokens that absorb disproportionate attention mass, stabilising the softmax distribution across layers.
Prepended learnable token whose final representation serves as an aggregate sequence embedding.
Linear projection turning non-overlapping image patches into token vectors for a transformer.
Extra learnable token added to vision transformers to absorb global computation and remove artefact activations.
Transformer block computing attention and feedforward branches simultaneously from the same normalised input, then summing.
Encoder-only transformer pretrained with masked-token and sentence-level objectives for contextual representations.
Decoder-only transformer family pretrained by next-token prediction on large text corpora.
Encoder-decoder transformer casting every task as text-to-text generation, using relative position bias.
Encoder-decoder transformer pretrained as a denoising autoencoder over corrupted text.
Transformer adding segment-level recurrence and relative positions to extend context beyond one window.
terms.n: Largely superseded by long-context decoder-only transformers with RoPE scaling.

terms.d: Transformer applied to sequences of image patch embeddings for visual recognition.
Hierarchical vision transformer computing attention in local windows that shift between successive layers.
Architecture cross-attending arbitrary-sized inputs into a fixed latent array processed by self-attention.
Mechanism injecting token order information into an otherwise permutation-equivariant attention architecture.
Fixed absolute encoding adding sine and cosine functions of position at geometrically spaced frequencies.
Trainable vector per position index added to token embeddings.
Scheme conditioning attention on the offset between query and key rather than absolute indices.
Learned scalar added to attention logits per bucketed relative distance, shared across layers.
Encoding that rotates query and key vectors by position-dependent angles, making dot products relative.
Context extension that rescales position indices so pretrained RoPE frequencies cover a longer window.
Context extension adjusting RoPE base frequency non-uniformly to preserve high-frequency resolution.
RoPE extension combining frequency-band-wise interpolation with attention temperature scaling for long contexts.
Encoding adding a head-specific linear penalty proportional to query-key distance directly to attention logits.
Decoder-only setup omitting explicit position signals, relying on causal masking to induce order.
Rotary encoding variant adding exponential decay per frequency to improve length extrapolation.
Encoding where position counters increment only on content-selected tokens, making positions context-dependent.
Attention where all heads share a single key and value projection, shrinking the KV cache.
terms.n: Mostly displaced by grouped-query attention, which retains more quality at similar cost.

terms.d: Attention where groups of query heads share one key-value head, interpolating between MHA and MQA.
Attention compressing keys and values into a low-rank latent cache decompressed per head at inference.
Design reusing one layer's key-value tensors across several subsequent layers to shrink cache memory.
Attention subtracting two softmax maps per head to cancel common-mode noise on irrelevant context.
Bounding attention or output logits with a scaled tanh to prevent numerical blow-up.
Attention restricting each query to a subset of keys, reducing quadratic cost to sub-quadratic.
Attention limiting each token to a fixed-width local neighbourhood of preceding positions.
Early sparse-attention model using fixed strided and block patterns over long sequences.
Transformer combining sliding-window local attention with a few designated globally attending tokens.
Sparse transformer mixing window, global and random attention patterns with theoretical universality guarantees.
Transformer grouping similar queries and keys by locality-sensitive hashing and attending only within buckets.
terms.n: Largely superseded in practice by IO-aware exact attention such as FlashAttention.

terms.d: Attention projecting the key and value sequence length to a fixed low rank, giving linear cost.
Attention approximating the softmax kernel with random features, enabling linear-time computation.
Attention approximating the softmax matrix by Nystrom sampling of landmark tokens.
Attention replacing softmax with a kernel feature map so computation becomes a running state update.
Linear attention adding data-dependent gating to the recurrent state, with a hardware-efficient chunked form.
Linear attention whose state update follows the delta rule, overwriting rather than only accumulating associations.
Linear attention combining the delta update rule with a learned decay gate on the recurrent state.
IO-aware exact attention kernel that tiles computation in on-chip memory and avoids materialising the attention matrix.
terms.n: Version 1 is superseded by FlashAttention-2 and the Hopper-optimised FlashAttention-3.

terms.d: Serving technique storing the KV cache in non-contiguous fixed-size blocks to eliminate memory fragmentation.
Distributed exact attention passing key-value blocks around a ring of devices to shard very long sequences.
Attention augmenting local attention with a compressive associative memory carried across segments.
Trainable sparse attention combining compressed coarse tokens, selected fine blocks and a local window.
Layer holding many parallel subnetworks where a router activates only a few per input.
Transformer feedforward layer replaced by many experts of which only top-scoring ones compute.
Small learned network scoring experts for each token and deciding which ones process it.
Routing rule dispatching each token to the k highest-scoring experts, combining their outputs by gate weights.
MoE transformer routing each token to exactly one expert to minimise routing and communication overhead.
Early sharded MoE transformer introducing top-2 routing, expert capacity limits and automatic model parallelism.
Inverted routing where each expert selects its top tokens, guaranteeing balanced expert load.
Expert always activated for every token, capturing common knowledge alongside sparsely routed specialists.
Splitting experts into many smaller ones so routing can compose more specialised combinations per token.
Training penalty encouraging routers to distribute tokens evenly across experts.
Balancing scheme adjusting per-expert routing bias from observed load instead of adding a gradient penalty.
Multiplier setting how many tokens each expert may accept per batch before overflow.
Discarding or passing through tokens routed to an expert that has exceeded its capacity.
Fully differentiable MoE where each expert processes weighted mixtures of all tokens rather than discrete assignments.
Architecture routing only a subset of tokens through each layer, making compute depth token-dependent.
Subset of a sparse model's weights actually used for a given token, versus total parameter count.
MoE design combining fine-grained routed experts with always-on shared experts.
Sequence model propagating a continuous-time linear latent state, computable as recurrence or convolution.
Framework deriving state matrices that optimally compress input history onto polynomial bases.
Deep SSM using a low-rank-corrected normal state matrix for stable, efficient long-range sequence modelling.
S4 simplification restricting the state matrix to a diagonal parameterisation.
SSM variant showing diagonal state matrices suffice to match structured-kernel performance.
Simplified SSM using a single multi-input multi-output layer computed by parallel associative scan.
Layer stacking shift and diagonal SSMs with multiplicative interactions to emulate associative recall.
Attention-free operator interleaving implicit long convolutions with elementwise multiplicative gating.
SSM whose state transition and input parameters are functions of the current token, enabling content-based forgetting.
Sequence architecture built from selective SSM blocks with a hardware-aware parallel scan.
Mamba successor with a scalar-times-identity state structure, formulated through state space duality for faster training.
Theoretical equivalence linking structured SSM recurrences to masked-attention matrix multiplications.
Primitive computing a linear recurrence in logarithmic depth by combining partial results associatively.
Sequence architecture with a decay-weighted retention operator supporting parallel, recurrent and chunkwise computation modes.
Recurrent architecture with transformer-style training parallelism, alternating time-mixing and channel-mixing blocks.
RWKV generation using a generalised delta-rule state update with vector-valued decay and in-context learning rates.
RWKV's paired blocks that combine information across positions and across feature channels respectively.
Simplified deep linear recurrence with complex diagonal state and exponential parameterisation, matching SSM performance.
Sequence layer whose hidden state is a small model's weights updated by gradient steps during inference.
Network computing node, edge or graph representations by iteratively exchanging information along graph edges.
General GNN formulation with per-edge message, per-node update and graph-level readout functions.
Step combining a node's neighbours' features with a permutation-invariant operator such as sum or mean.
Permutation-invariant pooling that turns node representations into a single graph-level vector.
GNN averaging neighbour features with symmetric degree normalisation, derived from a first-order spectral approximation.
GNN defining convolution through graph Laplacian eigenbasis, approximated by Chebyshev polynomial filters.
Inductive GNN sampling a fixed number of neighbours and aggregating them with learned functions.
GNN weighting neighbour contributions by learned attention coefficients.
Graph attention variant reordering the scoring computation to make attention genuinely dynamic per query node.
GNN using sum aggregation and an MLP, maximally expressive among message-passing networks.
Colour-refinement algorithm for graph isomorphism that upper-bounds the expressive power of message-passing GNNs.
Failure mode where repeated aggregation makes deep GNN node representations converge to indistinguishable values.
Failure mode where information from exponentially many distant nodes is compressed into fixed-size messages through bottleneck edges.
Learned hierarchical coarsening that assigns nodes to clusters, producing progressively smaller graphs.
Architecture applying global self-attention over nodes, using structural and positional encodings for graph topology.
Framework combining local message passing, global attention and positional or structural encodings in one layer.
Graph position feature built from eigenvectors of the graph Laplacian.
GNN with type-specific parameters for graphs containing multiple node and edge types.
GNN whose outputs rotate and translate with the input coordinates, preserving Euclidean symmetry.
Attention-based graph network equivariant to 3D rotations and translations via spherical-harmonic filters.
Library implementing graph neural network layers, sampling and batching on PyTorch.
Framework-agnostic library for building and scaling graph neural networks.
Network trained to reconstruct its input through a lower-capacity intermediate representation.
The compressed representation space in which an autoencoder or generative model's codes live.
Autoencoder trained to reconstruct clean inputs from deliberately corrupted versions.
Autoencoder with an overcomplete latent layer penalised toward few simultaneously active units.
Latent-variable generative model pairing an inference encoder with a decoder, trained by variational inference.
Variational objective combining reconstruction likelihood with KL divergence from latent prior to approximate posterior.
Sampling latents as a deterministic function of parameters and independent noise so gradients flow through.
Failure mode where the VAE's approximate posterior matches the prior and latents carry no information.
VAE weighting the KL term above one to encourage more disentangled latent factors.
VAE whose encoder and decoder are additionally conditioned on observed labels or attributes.
Autoencoder quantising encoder outputs to entries of a learned discrete codebook before decoding.
Finite set of learned embedding vectors to which continuous representations are quantised.
Quantisation applying successive codebooks to the residual error of previous stages.
Codebook-free quantisation rounding each latent dimension to a small fixed set of scalar levels.
Discrete autoencoder combining vector quantisation with adversarial and perceptual losses for sharp reconstructions.
Self-supervised vision transformer reconstructing heavily masked image patches from the visible subset.
Generative framework training a generator against a discriminator in a two-player minimax game.
GAN network mapping latent noise to samples intended to be indistinguishable from real data.
GAN network scoring whether a sample is real or generated, providing the generator's training signal.
GAN failure where the generator produces limited sample variety, ignoring parts of the data distribution.
Convolutional GAN establishing architectural conventions: strided convolutions, batch normalisation and no fully connected layers.
GAN whose generator and discriminator both receive an auxiliary conditioning input such as a class label.
GAN minimising an approximated Earth-mover distance using a Lipschitz-constrained critic.
Wasserstein GAN enforcing the Lipschitz constraint by penalising critic gradient norm instead of clipping weights.
GAN replacing the log loss with least-squares objectives to stabilise gradients.
Weight normalisation dividing by the largest singular value to bound a discriminator's Lipschitz constant.
Training scheme adding generator and discriminator layers incrementally to reach high resolutions.
terms.n: Superseded by StyleGAN2's skip and residual design, which removed progressive growing.

terms.d: GAN generating from a mapped latent style vector injected through adaptive instance normalisation at each resolution.
StyleGAN revision using weight demodulation, skip generators and path-length regularisation to remove droplet artefacts.
StyleGAN revision redesigning signal processing to make generation translation and rotation equivariant, eliminating texture sticking.
Layer replacing feature statistics with scale and bias predicted from a style vector.
Large-scale class-conditional GAN using orthogonal regularisation and the truncation trick for high-fidelity images.
Conditional GAN for paired image-to-image translation with a U-Net generator and reconstruction loss.
Fully convolutional discriminator classifying overlapping local patches rather than whole images.
Unpaired image translation framework with two generators constrained by cycle-consistency reconstruction losses.
Single generator performing multi-domain image translation conditioned on a target domain label.
GAN maximising mutual information between a subset of latent codes and generated samples to induce interpretable factors.
GAN whose discriminator is an autoencoder assigning low reconstruction energy to real samples.
Generative model transforming a simple base distribution through invertible maps with tractable exact likelihood.
Identity relating transformed and base densities through the Jacobian determinant of the invertible map.
Invertible layer transforming one half of the variables with parameters computed from the untouched half.
First coupling-based flow, using purely additive couplings with unit Jacobian determinant.
Flow extending NICE with affine couplings, multi-scale architecture and masked convolutions.
Flow adding invertible 1x1 convolutions and activation normalisation to affine coupling architectures.
Learned channel permutation generalisation whose log-determinant is computed from an LU-factorised weight matrix.
Flow stacking autoregressive transforms with fast density evaluation and sequential sampling.
Flow inverting the autoregressive direction to give fast sampling and slow density evaluation.
Flow using monotonic rational-quadratic spline transforms for expressive, analytically invertible elementwise maps.
Flow defining the transformation as an ordinary differential equation integrated over continuous time.
Model parameterising a hidden state's time derivative by a network and solving it with an ODE solver.
Continuous flow using stochastic trace estimation to compute log-density changes without restricting the network.
Transformer-based autoregressive normalising flow demonstrating competitive likelihoods and sample quality at scale.
Generative model that learns to reverse a gradual noising process, denoising samples step by step.
Fixed Markov chain or SDE that progressively adds noise until data becomes approximately Gaussian.
Function setting how much noise is added at each diffusion timestep.
Discrete-time diffusion model trained to predict the noise added at each step.
Non-Markovian deterministic sampler letting a trained diffusion model generate in far fewer steps.
Generative model learning the gradient of the log data density at each noise level.
Deterministic ordinary differential equation sharing marginal distributions with a diffusion SDE, enabling exact likelihoods.
Sampling method steering diffusion trajectories with gradients from a separately trained noisy-input classifier.
Sampling method extrapolating between conditional and unconditional model predictions to strengthen conditioning.
Diffusion model operating in a pretrained autoencoder's compressed latent space rather than pixel space.
Diffusion backbone replacing the U-Net with a transformer over latent patches, conditioned via adaptive normalisation.
Multimodal diffusion transformer using separate weight streams for text and image tokens with joint attention.
Unified diffusion design framework specifying preconditioning, noise distribution and sampler as separable choices.
Generative model trained so any point on a trajectory maps directly to its origin, enabling one-step sampling.
Generative model learning straight-line transport between noise and data by regressing constant velocity.
Procedure retraining a rectified flow on its own generated pairs to straighten trajectories further.
Simulation-free training that regresses a network onto the velocity field of a prescribed probability path.
Tractable flow-matching objective regressing velocities of per-sample conditional paths instead of the intractable marginal field.
Framework defining generative transport by interpolating between two distributions, unifying diffusion and flow-based models.
Diffusion over categorical data whose forward process progressively masks or corrupts discrete tokens.
Adapter cloning a diffusion backbone's encoder to inject spatial conditioning through zero-initialised connections.
Model defining an unnormalised density through a learned scalar energy assigned to each configuration.
Scalar network output whose low values correspond to high-probability configurations.
Normalising constant summing or integrating the exponentiated negative energy over all configurations.
Training approximation contrasting data statistics with those of short Markov chains started from data.
Sampling procedure following the energy gradient with added Gaussian noise at each step.
Fully connected stochastic binary network whose distribution is defined by a quadratic energy.
Bipartite energy-based model with visible and hidden layers and no intra-layer connections.
terms.n: Historical; superseded by backpropagation-trained deep networks and modern generative models.

terms.d: Generative model of stacked RBMs trained greedily layer by layer.
terms.n: Historical; superseded by end-to-end deep supervised and generative training.

terms.d: Recurrent associative memory storing patterns as energy minima recovered by iterative state updates.
Continuous associative memory with exponential storage capacity whose retrieval rule equals transformer attention.
Network representing a signal as a continuous function from coordinates to field values.
Small fully connected network taking spatial or spatiotemporal coordinates as its only input.
Encoding coordinates through sinusoids at multiple frequencies so networks can fit high-frequency detail.
Implicit representation network using periodic sine activations with principled weight initialisation.
Neural field regressing a signed distance function to represent shape surfaces as a zero level set.
Neural field predicting whether each queried 3D point lies inside a shape.
Neural field mapping position and view direction to colour and density, rendered by differentiable volume integration.
terms.n: Largely displaced for real-time novel-view synthesis by 3D Gaussian splatting.

terms.d: Differentiable compositing of colour and density samples along camera rays to form a pixel.
Feature encoding indexing trainable vectors in multi-level hash tables, enabling very fast neural field training.
Explicit scene representation of anisotropic 3D Gaussians rasterised differentiably for real-time novel-view synthesis.
Additive shortcut adding a layer's input to its output, easing gradient flow through depth.
Residual block applying normalisation and activation before the convolutions, giving a clean identity path.
Residual block reducing channels with 1x1 convolution, filtering, then restoring width.
Deep feedforward network with learned gates mixing transformed and carried-through signals.
Regulariser randomly dropping whole residual branches during training, shortening the effective network.
Architecture combining convolutional stages for local features with attention stages for global context.
Vision architecture stacking depthwise convolution stages before relative-attention transformer stages.
Speech architecture inserting a convolution module inside each transformer block between two feedforward halves.
Hybrid language model interleaving Mamba and attention layers with mixture-of-experts feedforward blocks.
Hybrid model alternating selective state space layers with sliding-window attention for efficient long-context recall.
Hybrid model using a Mamba backbone with a shared global attention module reused across depth.
Small-model architecture running Mamba and attention heads in parallel within the same layer.
Hybrid architecture mixing gated linear recurrences with periodic local attention layers.
Purely recurrent architecture built from gated linear recurrent blocks without any attention layers.

uncertain: Lightning attention (MiniMax-01) and DeepSeek sparse attention (DSA) appear in secondary 2025-2026 sources; I could not verify their canonical definitions or continued use, so they are omitted from terms.
Liquid-S4 and Mega-S4 appear in SSM survey listings; their independent status versus being survey-only groupings is unverified.
KERPLE and other kernelised relative-position biases are real published methods, but current adoption in 2026 models is unverified.
DeltaProduct (Householder-product state updates in linear RNNs) is published but I could not confirm whether it is established enough for a core glossary.

Bayesian flow networks and cold diffusion are real published variants; whether they remain distinct categories in the current diffusion taxonomy, rather than being folded into discrete diffusion and generalised corruption, is unverified.
Production hybrid Mamba-Transformer model lines such as Nemotron-H and Falcon-H1 are referenced in 2025-2026 material; exact naming and current status not verified.
Whether Reformer, Linformer and Performer should carry deprecation notes is a judgement call: they are still cited academically but rarely used in production, where FlashAttention plus GQA dominate.
Exact 2026 status of FlashAttention-3 beyond Hopper-generation GPUs (for example Blackwell support) was not verified.

terms.d: The field concerned with computational methods for representing, analysing, generating and understanding human language.
The principle that words occurring in similar contexts carry similar meanings, underpinning all corpus-derived vector representations.
The study of internal word structure and the rules by which words are formed from smaller meaning-bearing units.
The smallest linguistic unit carrying meaning or grammatical function, either a root or an affix.
The system of rules governing how words combine into phrases, clauses and grammatical sentences.
The study of literal meaning of words, phrases and sentences independent of speaker context.
Assigning each token a grammatical category label such as noun, verb, adjective or determiner.
Detecting text spans denoting entities and classifying them into types such as person, organisation or location.
Mapping a recognised entity mention to its unique record in a knowledge base or ontology.
Identifying semantic relationships holding between pairs of entities mentioned in text.
Producing a tree of directed head-dependent grammatical relations between the words of a sentence.
Producing a hierarchical phrase-structure tree that groups words into nested syntactic constituents.
Labelling sentence arguments with their roles relative to a predicate, such as agent, patient or instrument.
Grouping mentions across a text that refer to the same real-world entity.
Selecting which dictionary sense of an ambiguous word is intended in a given context.
Classifying whether a hypothesis sentence is entailed by, contradicts, or is neutral toward a premise.
Scoring how close in meaning two texts are, usually on a graded numeric scale.
Unsupervised discovery of latent themes in a corpus as distributions over words and documents.
A discriminative sequence model scoring whole label sequences jointly, long standard for tagging and span extraction.
Converting raw text into a canonical surface form before further processing.
Applying NFC, NFD, NFKC or NFKD forms so equivalent character sequences share one byte representation.
Mapping characters to a single case so that surface case differences do not create distinct tokens.
High-frequency function words removed from sparse representations because they carry little discriminative signal.
Heuristically truncating word forms to a common stem using suffix-stripping rules, without guaranteeing a real word.
Mapping inflected word forms to their dictionary headword using morphological analysis and part-of-speech information.

An initial split of text on whitespace, punctuation or regex patterns before a subword algorithm is applied.
Removing repeated or highly similar documents from a corpus, typically via hashing or shingle overlap.
Splitting a document into passages sized for embedding and retrieval.
Cutting text into equal-length windows that share a margin of tokens with their neighbours.
Choosing chunk boundaries where consecutive sentence embeddings diverge, rather than at fixed lengths.
Converting a text string into a sequence of discrete units drawn from a fixed vocabulary.
One discrete vocabulary unit produced by a tokeniser and mapped to a single integer identifier.
Treating whole whitespace-delimited words as vocabulary units, producing large vocabularies and frequent unknown tokens.
Treating individual characters as vocabulary units, giving tiny vocabularies and very long sequences.
Treating raw UTF-8 bytes as base units, so any input is representable with a 256-symbol alphabet.
Splitting words into frequent fragments so that rare words decompose into known pieces.
A tokenisation algorithm that repeatedly merges the most frequent adjacent symbol pair until a target vocabulary size.
BPE trained over raw bytes rather than characters, removing unknown tokens entirely.
A subword algorithm choosing merges that maximise training-corpus likelihood, and segmenting by greedy longest match.
A subword method that prunes an oversized candidate vocabulary by expected likelihood loss under a unigram model.

OpenAI's fast byte-level BPE tokeniser library exposing the encodings used by its models.
A Rust-backed library implementing BPE, WordPiece and Unigram with normalisation, pre-tokenisation and alignment pipelines.
The ordered list of learned symbol-pair merges that defines how a BPE tokeniser segments text.
A segmentation strategy that repeatedly consumes the longest vocabulary entry matching the remaining input.
Dynamic-programming search for the highest-probability segmentation under a unigram subword model.
Sampling alternative valid segmentations during training so the model becomes robust to tokenisation variation.
Randomly skipping merge operations at training time to generate varied BPE segmentations of the same word.
Encoding characters absent from a subword vocabulary as their constituent byte tokens instead of an unknown symbol.
A reserved vocabulary entry carrying structural meaning rather than text content, such as padding or sequence boundaries.
An architecture consuming characters or bytes directly, with no learned discrete vocabulary between text and model.
A byte-level text-to-text transformer that operates on UTF-8 bytes without any subword vocabulary.

A two-stage BPE variant that additionally learns tokens spanning whitespace, cutting sequence length substantially.
The finite set of tokens a tokeniser can emit and a model can embed or predict.
The number of entries in a tokeniser's vocabulary, trading sequence length against embedding and softmax cost.

The average number of tokens a tokeniser produces per word, measuring segmentation efficiency for a language.
Mean characters covered by each emitted token, a compression measure comparable across scripts.
The learned lookup table mapping each vocabulary identifier to its dense input vector.
Sharing one parameter matrix between the input embedding table and the output prediction layer.
Initialising embeddings for a new tokeniser's entries from an existing model's embeddings, usually by weighted averaging.
Adding new tokens to a trained model's vocabulary and embedding table to cover a domain or language.
A vocabulary entry rarely produced by the tokeniser in practice, whose embedding stays near its initialisation.
A representation counting term occurrences in a document while discarding word order.
A contiguous sequence of n tokens used as a single feature or language-model unit.

The count or normalised rate at which a term occurs within a single document.

A probabilistic lexical ranking function with saturating term frequency and document length normalisation.
