Expanding a query with terms drawn from its own top-ranked initial results.

Retrieving documents written in a language different from the query's language.
A fixed-length array of real numbers in which nearly every dimension carries value.
The number of components in an embedding vector, setting storage cost and representational capacity.
Rescaling a vector to unit Euclidean length so inner product equals cosine similarity.
The cosine of the angle between two vectors, measuring direction agreement independently of magnitude.
The sum of elementwise products of two vectors, a similarity that rewards both alignment and magnitude.
The straight-line L2 distance between two points in the embedding space.
The count of differing positions between two equal-length binary codes.

Negatives obtained free of cost from the other examples present in the same training batch.

Retrieving high-scoring non-relevant items with the current or an auxiliary model to build training negatives.

Yahoo Japan's neighbourhood graph and tree library for high-dimensional approximate nearest neighbour search.

Best-first search over a proximity graph that keeps a bounded candidate list and stops when it stops improving.
NVIDIA's GPU-native proximity graph index for high-throughput approximate nearest neighbour search.
Google's ANN library combining partitioning, anisotropic quantisation and exact rescoring.
Meta's library of CPU and GPU vector index implementations covering flat, IVF, PQ and graph structures.
Replacing vectors with short codes drawn from learned representative values to cut memory and distance cost.
The learned table of representative vectors whose indices form a quantised code.
Compressing each dimension independently to a low-precision integer using a per-dimension range.

Reducing each dimension to a single sign bit so distances become popcount operations on bitstrings.
Splitting a vector into subvectors and encoding each with its own small codebook index.
Learning a rotation before product quantisation so variance is balanced across subspaces.
Encoding a vector as the sum of codewords drawn from several full-dimensional codebooks.
Applying successive quantisation stages, each encoding the error left by the previous stage.

Comparing an uncompressed query against compressed database codes using precomputed lookup tables.
Recomputing exact distances on a shortlist retrieved with compressed codes, restoring accuracy lost to quantisation.
Retrieving more approximate candidates than requested so that rescoring can recover the true top results.

The HNSW build-time candidate list size, controlling graph quality and index build cost.
The HNSW query-time candidate list size, the main dial trading latency against recall.
The number of clusters an IVF index partitions the dataset into.
The number of IVF clusters scanned per query, trading latency against recall.
The number of subvectors a product quantiser splits each vector into, setting code length.
The code width per subvector, fixing each subcodebook's size and the quantisation fidelity.
The beam width retained during DiskANN or Vamana graph traversal, controlling accuracy and I/O.
The Vamana slack factor governing how aggressively long diverse edges are retained during graph construction.
The multiple of k fetched from a compressed index before exact rescoring.
Ranking with high-dimensional term-weight vectors served through an inverted index.
Ranking by similarity between low-dimensional learned embeddings of query and document.
Neural prediction of term weights over the vocabulary, keeping inverted-index serving while learning expansion.
A learned sparse retriever projecting text onto the vocabulary with regularisation enforcing sparse expanded term weights.
A learned sparse model assigning a single scalar impact weight to each term of query and document.

A ColBERT revision using distillation, denoised hard negatives and residual compression of token vectors.
The optimised serving engine for ColBERTv2, pruning centroids and candidates to cut late-interaction latency.
A late-interaction retriever embedding rendered document page images directly, bypassing text extraction.
The late-interaction scoring operator summing, over query tokens, the maximum similarity against any document token.
Combining lexical and dense retrieval signals into a single ranked list.
Conditioning a generative model on passages fetched at inference time from an external corpus.
A pipeline where a cheap recall-oriented retriever produces candidates that an expensive scorer reorders.
Ranking by having a sequence model directly generate document identifiers instead of scoring an index.
Retrieval that embeds a model-generated hypothetical answer instead of the raw query.
Prepending a model-written summary of the parent document to each chunk before indexing it.
Merging several ranked lists of the same candidates into one consensus ordering.
Fusion summing one over a constant plus rank across lists, needing no score normalisation.
Fusion adding each document's normalised scores across the lists that returned it.
Fusion taking a weighted average of normalised retriever scores with weights summing to one.
Rescaling incomparable retriever scores onto a common range before score-based fusion.
Reordering a retrieved candidate set with a more expensive and accurate relevance model.
A reranker jointly encoding query and candidate in one pass to emit a relevance score.
A pointwise BERT cross-encoder that classifies each query-passage pair as relevant or not.
A sequence-to-sequence reranker scoring relevance by the probability of generating a target word.
Prompting a language model to output an ordering over a window of candidates rather than per-item scores.
A hosted cross-encoder reranking API scoring query-document pairs across many languages.
BAAI's open cross-encoder reranker family, including lightweight and LLM-based variants.
A selection rule balancing relevance against redundancy with already-chosen results to diversify a ranking.
The fraction of the top k returned results that are relevant.
The fraction of all relevant documents that appear within the top k results.
The mean over queries of one divided by the rank of the first relevant result.
The mean across queries of average precision, itself the mean of precision values at each relevant rank.

Discounted cumulative gain divided by its value under the ideal ranking, giving a zero-to-one score.
The human-assigned labels marking which documents are relevant to which queries in an evaluation set.
A heterogeneous benchmark suite measuring zero-shot retrieval quality across many domains and task types.

Attention computed in several parallel subspaces with separate projections, concatenated and mixed by an output projection.
Attention variant where all heads share one key and value projection, shrinking the key-value cache.
Attention where groups of query heads share key-value heads, interpolating between multi-head and multi-query.
Attention compressing keys and values into a low-rank latent vector cached instead of full per-head tensors.
Attention restricted to a fixed span of recent tokens, giving linear cost in sequence length.
Initial tokens that absorb disproportionate attention mass and must be retained for stable streaming generation.
Position-wise two-layer network after attention holding most transformer parameters and much factual capacity.
Gated feed-forward activation combining a Swish-gated branch with a linear branch, standard in modern decoders.
Normalisation dividing activations by their root-mean-square without mean subtraction, cheaper than layer normalisation.
Placing normalisation before each sublayer so residual paths stay unnormalised, improving deep-network training stability.
Normalising query and key vectors before attention scoring to prevent logit growth and training divergence.
Additive channel carrying representations through layers, which each sublayer reads from and writes into.
Relative position encoding rotating query and key vectors by angles proportional to absolute position.
Position method adding a linear distance-proportional penalty to attention scores instead of positional embeddings.
Decoder trained without explicit position signals, relying on causal masking to induce order information.
Stored per-layer keys and values for past tokens, letting each new token be generated without recomputation.
Sharing the input embedding matrix with the output projection to cut parameters and regularise.
Layer holding many expert networks where a router activates a small subset per token.
Router rule sending each token to its k highest-scoring experts in a mixture-of-experts layer.
Always-active expert in a mixture-of-experts layer capturing common computation the routed experts need not duplicate.
Balancing expert utilisation by adjusting per-expert routing biases rather than adding a balancing loss term.
Distinction between parameters used per token and parameters stored, diverging sharply in sparse mixture-of-experts models.
Final linear projection mapping hidden states to vocabulary-sized logits before the softmax.
Unnormalised per-token scores over the vocabulary produced before softmax conversion into probabilities.
Model interleaving attention layers with recurrent state-space layers to cut long-sequence memory and compute.
Training objective adding heads that predict several future tokens, improving representations and enabling faster drafting.
Pretraining task of maximising the likelihood of each observed token given its predecessors.
Training regime feeding ground-truth prefixes rather than model outputs when predicting the next token.
Negative log-likelihood of the correct token under the predicted distribution, the standard pretraining loss.
Exponentiated average token loss, measuring how surprised a model is by held-out text.
Pretraining transformation reordering documents into prefix, suffix, middle so the model learns infilling.
Denoising objective masking contiguous token spans and training the model to regenerate them.
Pretraining recipe combining several corruption regimes with mode tokens signalling which denoising task applies.
Further next-token training of an existing base model on new domain or language data.
Stage between bulk pretraining and post-training that upweights high-quality, reasoning or long-context data.
Chosen sampling proportions across corpora sources that shape a pretrained model's capability profile.
Removing exact or near-duplicate documents from a corpus to reduce memorisation and wasted compute.
Scoring web documents with a trained classifier and keeping only high-scoring text for pretraining.
Detecting and removing evaluation-set text from training corpora to keep benchmark scores meaningful.
Public repeated web crawl that underlies most large-scale language model pretraining corpora.
Heuristically cleaned English Common Crawl subset released with T5 and widely reused.
Curated 800GB English corpus mixing academic, code, web and book sources for open pretraining.
Web-only pretraining corpus built by aggressive filtering and deduplication of Common Crawl.
Open three-trillion-token English corpus released with its full curation pipeline and toolkit.
Large filtered Common Crawl corpus and its educational-quality subset selected by classifier scoring.
Benchmark and corpus for comparing pretraining data curation strategies under fixed compute.
Common Crawl derivative combining classifier ensembling with synthetic rephrasing to enlarge high-quality token supply.
Open reproductions of the LLaMA pretraining mixture, the latter deduplicated and reduced.
Model-generated or model-rephrased text added to corpora to raise quality or extend scarce domains.
Concatenating short examples into full-length training sequences to avoid wasting compute on padding.
Learning-rate schedule holding a constant plateau then decaying, allowing checkpoints without a fixed token budget.
Parametrisation letting optimal hyperparameters transfer from small proxy models to much larger ones.
Empirical power-law relating model loss to parameters, data and compute across orders of magnitude.
Early scaling study concluding that model size should grow much faster than dataset size.
terms.n: Superseded for compute allocation by the Chinchilla scaling laws.

terms.d: Finding that parameters and training tokens should scale roughly proportionally for a fixed compute budget.
Allocating a fixed training compute budget between model size and tokens to minimise final loss.
Training tokens divided by parameters, the headline knob distinguishing compute-optimal from deliberately overtrained models.
Training a smaller model far past compute-optimal token counts to lower serving cost per query.
Choosing model size and training length to minimise total cost including expected lifetime inference.
Sweeping model sizes at equal compute budgets and fitting the loss minimum to derive scaling exponents.
Total floating-point operations consumed by a training run, approximated as six times parameters times tokens.
Capabilities absent in smaller models that appear abruptly above some scale threshold.
Argument that apparent capability jumps are artefacts of discontinuous metrics rather than genuine phase transitions.
Delayed generalisation where validation performance jumps long after training loss has already converged.
Scaling fit allowing smoothly joined power-law segments to capture inflections single power laws miss.
Projected exhaustion of high-quality human text, forcing reliance on synthetic data or repeated epochs.
Empirical relation between accuracy and inference compute spent on longer or repeated generation.
Relation predicting student performance from teacher quality, student size and distillation token budget.
Maximum number of tokens a model can attend over in one forward pass.
Span over which a model actually retains accuracy, typically shorter than its advertised window.
Extending context by linearly compressing position indices into the range seen during pretraining.
Context extension scaling rotary frequencies unevenly so high-frequency dimensions keep their resolution.
Rotary extension combining frequency-dependent interpolation with attention temperature adjustment, needing little continued training.
Context extension searching non-uniform rotary rescaling factors, later versions reaching million-token windows cheaply.
Additional training on long documents after rescaling positions so the model uses the extended window.
Distributed exact attention passing key-value blocks around a device ring, scaling sequence length with device count.
Computing attention in tiles over query and key blocks to bound memory without changing results.
Inference scheme keeping a few sink tokens plus a recent window to generate indefinitely at fixed memory.
Attending to a selected subset of positions rather than all, cutting long-sequence cost.
Storing cached keys and values at reduced precision to fit longer contexts in memory.
Dropping cache entries judged unimportant, by heavy-hitter or attention-score heuristics, to bound memory.
Serving technique storing the key-value cache in fixed pages, eliminating fragmentation and enabling sharing.
Reusing already-computed key-value state for a shared prompt prefix across requests or turns.
Splitting long prompt processing into chunks interleaved with decoding to keep latency steady.
The two inference phases: compute-bound parallel prompt processing, then memory-bound one-token-at-a-time generation.
Tendency of models to use information at context edges better than information buried centrally.
Degradation of reliability as context fills, even well below the nominal window limit.
Long-context probe inserting a fact at varied depths and checking exact retrieval.
Synthetic long-context benchmark spanning retrieval, tracing, aggregation and question answering at configurable lengths.
Multi-task bilingual benchmark for realistic long-document understanding and summarisation.
Updating every model weight on new data, giving maximum plasticity at maximum memory cost.
Training on curated prompt-response pairs with the standard token loss to shape output behaviour.
Fine-tuning on diverse instruction-following examples so a base model responds to natural-language directives.
Tokenisation convention with role markers and special tokens defining how conversations are serialised for a model.
Computing training loss on assistant tokens only, excluding prompt tokens from the objective.
Continued unsupervised training on in-domain text before task fine-tuning to shift the model's distribution.
Loss of previously learned capability when fine-tuning shifts weights toward a narrow new distribution.
Bootstrapping instruction data by prompting a model to generate and filter its own tasks.
Iteratively rewriting seed instructions into harder or more constrained variants to build difficulty-graded training sets.
Sampling many candidates, keeping those a filter or verifier accepts, and fine-tuning on them.
Claim that post-training mainly selects response style, so few high-quality examples can suffice.
Large aggregated set of academic tasks reformatted as instructions for multitask instruction tuning.
Family of methods adapting a frozen model by training a small number of added or selected parameters.
Trading compute for memory by recomputing activations during backward instead of storing them.
Computing in low precision while keeping master weights and reductions in higher precision for stability.
Distributed training that shards parameters, gradients and optimiser state across devices, gathering them only when needed.
Optimiser-state, gradient and parameter partitioning scheme removing memory redundancy in data-parallel training.
IO-aware exact attention kernel that tiles computation in fast memory, avoiding materialising the attention matrix.
Freezing base weights and learning a low-rank product added to selected weight matrices.
Inner dimension of the low-rank update, controlling adapter capacity and trainable parameter count.
Scaling constant dividing by rank that sets the effective magnitude of the low-rank update.
Set of base weight matrices chosen to receive adapters, commonly attention projections and feed-forward layers.
Folding trained low-rank matrices into base weights so inference carries no extra latency.
LoRA over a 4-bit quantised frozen base, with paged optimisers, enabling large-model tuning on one GPU.
Adaptation decomposing weights into magnitude and direction, applying low-rank updates only to direction.
LoRA variant assigning a much higher learning rate to the up-projection than the down-projection.
Rank-stabilised LoRA rescaling adapters by the square root of rank so high ranks train stably.
LoRA variant allocating rank budget adaptively across layers by pruning unimportant singular directions.
Adaptation freezing shared random projection matrices and training only small per-layer scaling vectors.
LoRA initialisation from the principal singular components of the pretrained weight, speeding convergence.
LoRA initialisation using minor singular components so adaptation avoids disturbing dominant pretrained directions.
LoRA initialisation using orthonormal factors derived from QR decomposition of the base weights.
Adapter factorising the update as a Hadamard product of two low-rank pairs for higher effective rank.
Adapter expressing the weight update as a Kronecker product of small matrices.
Generalised adapter learning scaling and shifting of weights and activations alongside low-rank terms.
LoRA variant freezing the down-projection and training only the up-projection to cut activation memory.
Adapter sharing low-rank matrices across layers, reducing trainable parameters further than standard LoRA.
Efficient context-extension fine-tuning combining shifted sparse attention with trainable embeddings and normalisation.
Quantisation-aware LoRA whose adapters fold back into a quantised model without dequantisation.
Adaptation jointly optimising a low-rank residual and a quantised base component of each weight matrix.
Pretraining-scale method accumulating a full-rank update by repeatedly training and merging fresh low-rank adapters.
Serving or training scheme routing tokens across several LoRA experts on one frozen base.
Serving system hosting thousands of LoRA adapters over a shared base with paged adapter memory.
Small down-projection, nonlinearity and up-projection inserted inside frozen transformer blocks and trained alone.
Adapter placed alongside rather than after a sublayer, so its output adds to the sublayer's.
Composition method learning attention over several trained task adapters to combine their knowledge.
Extreme parameter-efficient tuning updating only the model's bias terms.
Adaptation learning element-wise rescaling vectors applied to keys, values and feed-forward activations.
Prepending trainable key-value vectors to every attention layer while keeping all model weights frozen.
Learning continuous soft prompt embeddings prepended to the input, with the model entirely frozen.
Deep prompt tuning inserting trainable prompts at every layer, matching full tuning across scales.
Full-parameter training that projects gradients into a low-rank subspace to cut optimiser memory.
Post-training pipeline fitting a reward model to human preferences then optimising the policy against it.
Two responses to one prompt labelled chosen and rejected, the base unit of preference training data.
Clipped policy-gradient algorithm, long the default reinforcement learning optimiser for language model alignment.
Divergence term keeping the trained policy near a frozen reference model during reinforcement learning.
Frozen copy of the pre-alignment policy used to anchor divergence penalties or implicit reward ratios.
Learned critic estimating expected future reward from a partial generation, used for advantage estimation.
Bias-variance-traded advantage estimator combining multi-step returns with a learned value baseline.
Critic-free policy gradient using other sampled completions' rewards as each sample's baseline.
Critic-free reinforcement method using the greedy-decoded response's reward as the variance-reduction baseline.
Critic-free method sampling a group per prompt and normalising rewards within the group as advantages.
GRPO refinement with decoupled clipping, dynamic sampling and token-level loss for stable long reasoning training.
Group-relative method applying importance ratios and clipping at sequence level, stabilising mixture-of-experts reinforcement training.
Corrected GRPO removing length and standard-deviation normalisation biases that inflate response length.
Closed-form objective training directly on preference pairs, treating the policy itself as its implicit reward model.
DPO variant replacing the logistic link with a squared loss to curb overfitting to deterministic preferences.
Alignment objective learning from unpaired binary desirable or undesirable labels using a prospect-theory value function.
Single-stage method adding an odds-ratio preference penalty to the supervised loss, removing the reference model.
Reference-free objective using length-normalised average log-probability as implicit reward with a target margin.
Reference-free preference objective combining a contrastive term with a supervised anchor on chosen responses.
Preference method sourcing training pairs by rejection sampling from the estimated optimal policy.
Sequence-likelihood calibration using ranking and margin losses over human-feedback pairs instead of reinforcement learning.
Repeatedly sampling from the current policy, relabelling preferences, and re-running direct preference optimisation.
Training loop where the model judges its own generations to produce preference data for the next round.
Alignment where preference labels come from an AI judge rather than human annotators.
Alignment method where a model critiques and revises its own outputs against written principles, then trains on them.
Input and output filters trained on constitution-derived synthetic data to block disallowed content.
Training a reasoning model to recall and reason over written safety policies before answering.
Reinforcement training where reward comes from programmatic checking of answers rather than a learned reward model.
Automatically checkable success signal such as unit tests passing or an exact-match final answer.
Reward-ranked fine-tuning that samples candidates, keeps the top-scoring ones and trains on them iteratively.
Capability loss on general benchmarks incurred as a side effect of alignment post-training.
Tendency to agree with a user's stated view rather than maintain an accurate answer.
Three-part behavioural target framing what alignment training aims for in assistant models.
Adversarial probing of a model to elicit harmful or policy-violating behaviour before deployment.
Trained precedence ordering where system instructions outrank user text, which outranks tool or document content.
Model scoring candidate responses, trained to reproduce human or AI preference judgements.
Pairwise comparison model turning preference labels into a scalar reward via a logistic likelihood.
Reward model scoring only the final answer of a solution, ignoring intermediate steps.
Reward model scoring each intermediate reasoning step, enabling step-level search and credit assignment.
Judge model that produces a critique and verdict in text rather than emitting a scalar head output.
Policy exploiting flaws in the reward signal to score highly without achieving the intended behaviour.
Degradation of true quality as policy optimisation pushes past the reward model's reliable range.
Compressing a trained model's numerics without retraining, using at most a small calibration set.
Simulating low-precision arithmetic during training so weights adapt to quantisation error.
Recovering accuracy of a quantised student by distilling from the full-precision model.
Storing weights at low precision while computing in higher precision after dequantisation.
Reducing precision of intermediate tensors as well as weights, enabling low-precision matrix multiplication.
Shorthand for the bit widths chosen independently for weights and activations.
Assigning a separate scale factor to each small block of weights instead of whole tensors.
Small representative sample run through the model to collect activation statistics guiding quantisation.
Rare large-magnitude activation channels that dominate quantisation error in transformers.
Mixed-precision scheme keeping outlier channels in 16-bit while quantising the rest to 8-bit integers.
Migrating activation outlier difficulty into weights by per-channel rescaling, enabling 8-bit weight-activation inference.
One-shot layer-wise quantisation using approximate second-order information to compensate rounding error.
Activation-aware weight quantisation protecting the small fraction of channels most salient to activations.
Four-bit data type with levels information-theoretically optimal for normally distributed weights.
Quantising the quantisation constants themselves to shave further bits per parameter.
Library providing 8-bit and 4-bit quantised linear layers and paged optimisers for training and inference.
Single-file model container used by llama.cpp holding quantised weights, tokeniser and metadata.
Earlier llama.cpp model file format lacking extensible metadata.
terms.n: Deprecated; replaced by GGUF.

terms.d: llama.cpp quantisation family mixing bit widths across tensor types with block-wise super-scales.
llama.cpp codebook-based low-bit quantisations giving better quality than K-quants at very small sizes.
Per-weight importance statistics gathered from calibration text to steer llama.cpp quantisation.
ExLlamaV2 mixed-precision quantisation format allowing fractional average bits per weight.
terms.n: ExLlamaV2 is archived; superseded by ExLlamaV3 and the EXL3 format.

terms.d: ExLlamaV3 quantisation format with rotation-based coding, tensor parallelism and integrated speculative decoding.
Apple Silicon quantised weight format and runtime using unified memory on Mac hardware.
Half-quadratic quantisation that is calibration-free and fast, optimising a robust weight-reconstruction objective.
Two-bit-capable quantisation using incoherence-inducing random rotations plus lattice codebooks.
Additive quantisation mapping weight groups to sums of entries from multiple learned codebooks.
Sparse-quantised representation isolating outlier weights at high precision inside a low-bit tensor.
Dense-and-sparse quantisation combining sensitivity-weighted non-uniform clustering with a sparse outlier matrix.
Post-training quantisation learning clipping thresholds and equivalent transformations per layer by block-wise optimisation.
Rotation-based scheme applying Hadamard transforms to remove outliers, enabling end-to-end 4-bit inference.
Quantisation learning rotation matrices on the Stiefel manifold to minimise low-bit accuracy loss.
Eight-bit floating-point formats with hardware support, used for weights, activations and training.
Microscaling four-bit float with a shared power-of-two scale per block of thirty-two values.
Four-bit float with sixteen-value blocks and two-level scaling, giving better accuracy than MXFP4 on supporting hardware.
Sixteen-bit float with float32 exponent range, the default training and reference-inference precision.
Architecture training weights natively as ternary values, replacing most multiplications with additions.
Training a smaller student to reproduce a larger teacher's outputs or internal signals.
Student trained on teacher-generated text with the ordinary token loss, ignoring teacher probabilities.
Matching the student's full output distribution to the teacher's soft probabilities per token.
Training the student on teacher-decoded sequences rather than per-token distributions.
Distillation where the teacher scores sequences sampled from the student, fixing exposure bias.
On-policy distillation framework mixing student-sampled data with flexible divergence choices between teacher and student.
Distillation minimising reverse Kullback-Leibler divergence so the student avoids overestimating low-probability teacher regions.
Fine-tuning a smaller model on a reasoning model's chains of thought to transfer problem-solving behaviour.
Internalising a long prompt or scaffold by training the model to match its outputs without that context.
Distilling a model into a copy of itself, often to consolidate behaviours or recover from compression.
Removing whole heads, channels or layers so the smaller model runs faster on standard hardware.
Zeroing individual weights by importance criteria, needing sparse kernels to realise speedups.
One-shot pruning solving layer-wise reconstruction to reach high sparsity without retraining.
Pruning by weight magnitude times input activation norm, requiring no weight update or retraining.
Dropping whole transformer layers judged redundant, then healing the model with brief further training.
Compression recipe pruning a large model along several axes then distilling to recover accuracy cheaply.
Selecting the highest-probability token at each step, giving deterministic but often repetitive output.
Maintaining several partial sequences ranked by cumulative likelihood and expanding the best each step.
Scalar dividing logits before softmax, flattening or sharpening the sampling distribution.
Restricting sampling to the k highest-probability tokens after renormalising their probabilities.
Sampling from the smallest token set whose cumulative probability exceeds a threshold.
Keeping tokens whose probability exceeds a fraction of the top token's probability, adapting to confidence.
Truncation whose threshold scales with the square of the top token's probability.
Keeping tokens whose surprisal is closest to the distribution's entropy rather than simply most probable.
Truncation rules cutting tokens below an absolute or entropy-scaled probability floor.
Truncation keeping tokens whose logits lie within a set number of standard deviations of the maximum.
Feedback sampler adjusting truncation each step to hold generated text at a target perplexity.
Sampler probabilistically removing the most likely tokens when several are confident, increasing diversity.
Penalty suppressing tokens that would continue a repeated n-gram already present in the context.
Multiplicative logit reduction for tokens already appearing in the context.
Logit reduction proportional to how often a token has already appeared.
Flat logit reduction applied once a token has appeared at all, encouraging new topics.
Hard rule forbidding any n-gram from occurring twice in the generated text.
Fixed per-token offsets added to logits to force or forbid specific vocabulary items.
Sequence in which penalties and truncations are applied, which materially changes the resulting distribution.
Decoding balancing model confidence against a degeneration penalty measuring similarity to previous representations.
Choosing tokens by the difference between a strong model's and a weak model's log-probabilities.
Decoding by contrasting logits from later and earlier layers of the same model to improve factuality.
Generating several completions and returning the one a scorer or verifier ranks highest.
Selecting the candidate most similar on average to all other sampled candidates under a utility metric.
Strings that terminate generation when produced, bounding output beyond the end-of-sequence token.
Special token whose emission signals that the model considers the response complete.
Output variation at fixed seed and temperature caused by batching and non-associative floating-point reductions.
Acceleration where a cheap drafter proposes tokens that the target model verifies in one parallel pass.
Small fast model producing candidate continuations for a larger target model to accept or reject.
Fraction of drafted tokens the target model verifies, the main determinant of speculative speedup.
Speculative method attaching multiple parallel prediction heads to the target model instead of a separate drafter.
Speculative family drafting in the target model's feature space; EAGLE-3 conditions on multiple hidden layers.
Draft-model-free acceleration generating and verifying n-gram continuations in parallel via Jacobi iteration.
Drafting by copying n-gram continuations found in the prompt, effective for summarisation and editing.
Using a subset of the model's own layers as the drafter, then verifying with the full model.
Generated content that is unsupported by the source context or false about the world.
Output that directly contradicts information present in the provided source or context.
Output adding content absent from and unverifiable against the provided source.
Degree to which a response is entailed by the supplied context, independent of real-world truth.
Degree to which a response matches verified real-world facts, independent of the supplied context.
Fluent fabrication produced with high confidence and no signal of uncertainty.
Conditioning generation on retrieved or supplied evidence so claims can be traced to sources.
Linking specific generated statements to the exact supporting spans in source material.
Model declining to answer when evidence or internal confidence is insufficient.
Alignment between a model's stated or implicit confidence and its actual accuracy.
Uncertainty measure clustering sampled answers by meaning and computing entropy over the meaning clusters.
Black-box hallucination detection comparing multiple stochastic samples for mutual consistency.
Metric decomposing long-form output into atomic facts and scoring each against a knowledge source.
Benchmark of questions designed so imitation of common human misconceptions produces false answers.
Compounding error where an early fabricated claim forces the model to justify it with further fabrications.
Generating intermediate reasoning steps in text before producing a final answer.
Eliciting step-by-step reasoning with a trigger instruction rather than worked examples.
Prompting with exemplars that include their reasoning traces, not only their answers.
Automatically constructing reasoning exemplars by clustering questions and generating traces for representative members.
Sampling many reasoning paths and returning the answer that appears most often.
Decomposing a problem into ordered easier subproblems and solving them cumulatively.
Search over a tree of partial reasoning states with explicit expansion, evaluation and backtracking.
Reasoning framework letting thought nodes merge and be refined in a general graph rather than a tree.
Prompting that embeds an entire search procedure in one context, imitating exploration without repeated calls.
Producing an answer outline first, then expanding each point in parallel to reduce latency.
Reasoning expressed as executable code whose interpreter, not the model, computes the answer.
Separating reasoning into generated program steps and delegating all numeric computation to execution.
Loop where a model critiques its own output and rewrites it iteratively without extra training.
Agent pattern converting task failures into written self-reflections stored and reused on later attempts.
Having a model check its own answer, often by reworking the problem backwards from the result.
Several model instances argue and critique across rounds before converging on a final answer.

terms.t: Monte Carlo tree search for reasoning
terms.d: Guiding step-level generation with simulation, value backup and exploration bonuses over reasoning trees.
Bootstrapping by fine-tuning on self-generated reasoning traces that reached the correct answer.
Training a model to generate internal rationales at every token to improve next-token prediction.
Iterative loop alternating sampling with reward-filtered fine-tuning, framed as expectation-maximisation.
Extended reasoning traces exhibiting backtracking, verification and branching, typically induced by reinforcement training.
Tokens the model generates for internal deliberation, billed but usually hidden from the final answer.
Configurable cap on reasoning tokens allowed before the model must commit to an answer.
Test-time control that suppresses the end-of-thinking token or appends continuation words to lengthen reasoning.
Failure mode where additional reasoning degrades accuracy or calibration on problems already solved.
Model post-trained to spend inference compute on extended deliberation before answering.
Compute spent during inference on longer, repeated or searched generation rather than during training.
Spending inference compute by extending one trace versus sampling many traces and aggregating.
Expanding and pruning candidate reasoning steps using a process reward model or checker as the scoring function.
Prompting style constraining each reasoning step to a few tokens, cutting cost while keeping accuracy.
API parameter selecting how much deliberation a reasoning model performs before answering.
Reasoning emitted between tool calls so the model can deliberate on each observed result.
The full token sequence supplied to a model, including system, user and prior turns.
Highest-precedence instruction block setting persona, rules and output conventions for a conversation.
Instructing a task with no worked examples, relying on instruction tuning to generalise.
Including several input-output examples in the prompt to demonstrate the desired mapping.
Adapting behaviour from examples in the prompt alone, with no weight updates.
Choosing which demonstrations to include, by similarity, diversity or difficulty, to maximise few-shot accuracy.
Assigning the model a persona or expertise framing to shape tone and assumed knowledge.
Explicit markers separating instructions, data and examples so the model parses prompt sections reliably.
Splitting work across several sequential model calls whose outputs feed the next prompt.
Breaking a complex request into explicitly enumerated subtasks before any is attempted.
Pattern where the model poses and answers explicit follow-up questions before the final answer.
Pattern interleaving reasoning traces with tool actions and observations in a single loop.
Agent pattern planning all tool calls upfront, then executing and combining results, decoupling reasoning from observations.
Instructing the model to devise an explicit plan first and then execute it step by step.
Asking for the governing principle or general question before addressing the specific instance.
Drafting an answer, generating verification questions, answering them independently, then revising.
Framework where the model composes task-specific reasoning structures from a bank of atomic reasoning modules.
Having the model produce relevant background facts first and conditioning the answer on them.
Asking the model to restate and expand the question before answering it.
Using a model to write, critique or improve prompts rather than to solve the task directly.
Automatic instruction search generating candidate prompts and selecting by scored execution on held-out data.
Optimisation method where a model proposes new prompts from a trajectory of previous prompts and scores.
Prompt optimiser using reflective natural-language mutation with Pareto selection over evaluation traces.
Framework declaring pipelines as typed modules and compiling prompts or weights against a metric.
Shortening a prompt while preserving task-relevant information, by token pruning or learned summarisation.
Prompt compression toolkit using a small model's perplexity to drop low-information tokens.
Trained compact soft tokens that stand in for a long prompt's content during inference.
Reusing server-side computed state for a repeated prompt prefix, cutting latency and input cost.
Attack where text inside retrieved or user-supplied content is treated by the model as instructions.
Parameterised prompt string with variable slots filled at runtime, enabling versioning and testing.
Generation guaranteed to conform to a declared schema rather than merely requested to.
Setting forcing syntactically valid JSON output without enforcing any particular schema.
Restricting decoding so output validates against a supplied JSON Schema, including types and required fields.
Masking the next-token distribution each step to only tokens keeping the output valid under a formal constraint.
Constraining generation with a context-free grammar, such as llama.cpp's GBNF format.
Compiling constraints into an automaton whose state determines the allowed token mask.
Boolean vector over the vocabulary applied to logits to forbid tokens violating the active constraint.
Backing up over a partially matched token boundary so constrained output keeps canonical tokenisation.
Structured generation library compiling regular expressions and schemas into precomputed automaton token masks.
Library interleaving fixed template text with constrained generation and control flow in one program.
Rust Earley-parser constraint engine providing low-latency grammar-constrained decoding to multiple runtimes.
Grammar engine with precomputed context-independent token masks, the default structured-output backend in major serving stacks.
Library enforcing JSON Schema or regex output by filtering allowed tokens during generation.
Client library binding model calls to typed objects with validation and automatic retry on failure.
Declared function name, description and parameter schema the model fills to request a tool invocation.
Post-generation pattern validating output and re-prompting with the error until it parses.
Discipline of deciding what occupies the context window across a task's whole token lifecycle.
Explicit allocation of the window across system prompt, tools, history, retrieved data and output.
Replacing accumulated conversation or tool output with a condensed representation once the window fills.
Maintaining a continually updated summary of earlier turns instead of retaining the raw transcript.
Delegating subtasks to agents with their own windows so only their results enter the parent context.
Loading full content only when needed, holding lightweight identifiers such as paths in context meanwhile.
Persistent store outside the window that the model writes to and reads from across sessions.
Externalised working notes the model maintains so intermediate state survives context truncation.
Capping or summarising tool outputs before they enter context to prevent window exhaustion.
Persistence of an erroneous or malicious statement in context that corrupts all subsequent reasoning.
Degraded focus when irrelevant material in a long context competes with the actual task.
Combining several models' weights into one without additional training on their original data.
Difference between a fine-tuned model's weights and its base, representing a learned capability directionally.
Adding or subtracting task vectors on a shared base to compose or remove capabilities.
Averaging weights of multiple fine-tuning runs from one initialisation to improve robustness.
Spherical interpolation between two checkpoints' weights, following an arc rather than a straight line.
Merging that trims small task-vector entries, elects a dominant sign per parameter, then averages agreeing values.
Randomly dropping task-vector entries and rescaling survivors to reduce interference before merging.
Merging that masks both extreme and negligible task-vector entries to remove noise and outliers.
Merging that drops task-vector entries with magnitude-proportional probability before electing and rescaling.
Merging weighting each model's parameters by Fisher information as a curvature-aware importance estimate.
Merging solving a closed-form least-squares problem per linear layer using input activation statistics.
Searching merge coefficients and layer arrangements with evolutionary algorithms against a target metric.
Stacking layers from different checkpoints to build a deeper model with no shared width constraint.
Toolkit implementing the major merging algorithms with a declarative configuration format.
Discrete unit from the model's vocabulary; the atomic element of input, output and billing.
Segmenting text into units between characters and words so rare words decompose into known pieces.

uncertain: torchtune (PyTorch fine-tuning library): I could not verify its 2026 maintenance status, so I left it out rather than list it as current or mark it deprecated.
Jsonformer: a real early structured-output library, but I could not confirm it is still maintained in 2026, so it is omitted.
'Sleep-time compute' (pre-computing reasoning about context before a query arrives): appears to be genuine 2025 research but I could not confirm it is established enough to be a curriculum term.
Entropy-based / adaptive samplers of the 'entropix' community lineage and the 2025 'p-less sampling' proposal: real proposals, but I could not verify adoption in mainstream runtimes.
Classifier-free guidance applied to text LLMs: published research, but I could not confirm current practical use, so it is not listed.
'LoRAFactory' appeared in one 2026 secondary source as a modular LoRA-variant codebase; I could not verify it exists, so it is excluded.
V-STaR, Delta-LoRA, MoRA, HydraLoRA, SBoRA and MiSS are named in the LoRA/reasoning literature, but I could not verify enough about each to define them safely.
BCO (binary classifier optimisation) and several other 2025-2026 DPO derivatives exist in TRL-adjacent literature; I could not verify their canonical definitions, so they are omitted.
Relative standing of MXFP4 versus NVFP4 as the 2026 default 4-bit inference format is contested across sources; I stated only what each format is.
The claim that XGrammar is 'the default' structured-output backend across vLLM, SGLang and TensorRT-LLM comes from one secondary source; the definition I give avoids asserting default status.

uncertain: A vendor comparison page claimed OpenAI acquired promptfoo in 2025. I could not confirm this from a primary source, so promptfoo is listed without an ownership note.

EU Digital Omnibus: I confirmed the package exists as a Commission proposal touching the AI Act, but could not verify the specific proposed new dates for high-risk obligations (reportedly late 2027 / mid 2028) or its current legislative stage in August 2026. The artificialintelligenceact.eu implementation timeline still shows the unamended 2 August 2026 and 2 August 2027 dates.

New York RAISE Act: I believe a frontier-model safety bill was signed in New York in late 2025 with 2026 effect, but could not verify its final text or effective date, so it is omitted from the term list.
California SB 942 (AI Transparency Act): reportedly amended by AB 853, which may have shifted its effective date from January 2026 to August 2026. The definition given deliberately omits a date.
C2PA standardisation: C2PA specification versions have reportedly been submitted to ISO (ISO 22144). I could not confirm publication status, so no ISO number is given.
Model Card Toolkit: I could not verify whether the Google repository is still maintained in 2026; no deprecation note is attached.
Tumult Analytics: governance may have changed after the Tumult Labs team moved to another organisation. Listed without a note.
CrypTen: appears to have low recent activity and may be effectively unmaintained; no maintenance note attached because I could not confirm.
SplxAI: reportedly subject to an acquisition (Zscaler) in 2025. Unconfirmed, so listed with no ownership note.

Aim Security (reported Cato Networks acquisition) and Invariant Labs (reported Snyk acquisition) were omitted or listed without notes because the acquisitions could not be verified here; mcp-scan is attributed to Invariant Labs, which is correct regardless.
NIST AI RMF: NIST states AI RMF 1.0 is under revision as of 2026, but no version 2.0 has been published; a Critical Infrastructure Profile concept note was released April 2026.
MLCommons AILuminate version numbering in 2026 (safety benchmark v1.0, jailbreak benchmark v0.5 were the versions visible); a newer release may exist.

Protect AI product line: I am confident Palo Alto Networks acquired Protect AI and that Prisma AIRS is the successor platform, but the exact current status of the open-source projects (ModelScan, LLM Guard, Rebuff, huntr) under that ownership is unverified. They are listed as active without deprecation notes.

Several obscure open-source projects appearing in an aggregated awesome-list (e.g. NNterp, Overcomplete) were seen only in secondary sources; NNterp was omitted, Overcomplete was omitted, and only projects I could independently place were retained.
Whether Microsoft Counterfit is formally archived versus merely inactive could not be confirmed; the note states maintenance mode.
